title: Website
text:
The website (https://fesmc.github.io/FesmData/) is a Quarto site in docs/. Most pages include a README of the repository (the datasets, Remap/, Records/, shared/, Publish/, Figures/), so that they are written once, next to the code; the pages for users (Home, Download, Products, Domains, Datasets, Precision) are written in docs/. The menus are set in docs/_quarto.yml.
Some parts are generated by julia fesmdata.jl docs (Publish/site.jl, standard library only), and not tracked:








File
Contents
From




docs/_products.md
The table of the datasets on each domain, with their versions (Products)
registry/


docs/_downloads/<Dataset>.md
The files of each grid of a dataset, with their links (Downloads, at the end of its page)
registry/


docs/_datasets.md, docs/_records.md
The overview of the datasets by topic, and of the records
Publish/datasets.toml ([_site] topics), registry/


docs/_domains.md
The table of the domains (Domains)
shared/domains.toml, Topo/products.toml



Each dataset page ends with figures of its products, made from the released files on Levante (docs/figures/<Dataset>/, by julia fesmdata.jl figures <Dataset>, see below); only their galleries are committed, the figures are kept on gh-pages. The overview figures of the domains linked from the table of the domains are figures/Domains/<folder>_TOPO-<product>.png (julia fesmdata.jl figures Domains).
.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml renders the site and publishes it to the gh-pages branch (a single commit, with the figures taken from there) on every push to main that changes the docs, the READMEs, the registry, Publish or the definitions of the domains. To preview it locally:
julia fesmdata.jl docs
quarto preview docs

title: Website
text:
Gridded products
One figure per released product: a column per domain, on the finest grid with at most 800 cells along its longer side (e.g. ANT-8KM, GRL-PAL-4KM, NH-16KM, GLOBAL-0.5DEG), and a row per field, with a colour bar per row. The crops of a domain (Greenland, Laurentide, Eurasia) are shown only if the domain itself is not. Coastlines are the ice-free ocean margin of the topography of the domain on the same grid (the Topo product of the zones of Regions), and the Natural Earth coastline on global grids.
By default the field is the first of the product’s variables (or of its file), at:

21 ka and the present, for a time in years ago;
the last time of a CF time axis;
January and July of a monthly climatology;
the first value of other dimensions (depth, structure, …).

Integer variables are drawn as classes (named by flag_values and flag_meanings), others with the 2-98% range of their values on all panels, symmetric with a diverging colour map when they have both signs in similar amounts.
The figure table of a product in <Dataset>/remap.toml changes this:
figure = { variables = ["uxy_srf"], scale = "log10", colorrange = [1, 3000] }
figure = { select = { depth = [100, 300] }, colormap = "inferno" }







Key
Value




variables
fields shown, a row each


select
values of other dimensions, by dimension: a value or a list (a row each); nearest in each file


colormap
a Makie colour map (e.g. "viridis", "balance", "ice")


colorrange
[min, max]


scale
"log10"


hide
a value not drawn (e.g. 0)



colormap, colorrange, scale and hide can also be tables by variable, e.g. colormap = { z_bed = "oleron", H_ice = "ice" }.
figure = false leaves a product without a figure, e.g. the products of a dataset with many similar ones (Paleoclimate shows the LGM of each model only).

title: Website
text:
Records
One figure per product: maps of the sites on the domains that contain them (GRL-PAL, ANT, NH, each site on the first), and the data next to them: a line per site or region against time (timeSeries) or depth (profile), or the observations against their time (point with a time). Data at sites without a time or depth (e.g. GPS uplift rates) colour the sites. The variable is the first data variable on the sites; figure = { variable = "dD" } in <Dataset>/records.toml shows another.

title: Website
text:
Topo and Regions
Topo has a figure per domain, its products side by side (bed elevation and ice thickness, with colour ranges from the data of the domain: the bed centred on sea level where it reaches below, otherwise over the land elevations), and the bed around Jakobshavn Isbræ on grids of 1, 4 and 16 km (topo.jl). Regions has worked examples of the region codes, zones and basins (regions.jl), on the North and on Antarctica: snippets of Julia code, run in order to make their maps, and shown on the page with their output.

title: Website
text:
Overview of the domains
julia fesmdata.jl figures Domains makes an overview figure of each Topo product of each domain, docs/figures/Domains/<folder>_TOPO-<product>.png, linked from the table of the domains (Domains page; crops link to those of their domain): the bed and surface elevation and ice thickness of the product, the three levels of the regions (labelled by path and name), the zones and the basins of each basin set of the domain, on the finest grid with at most 1600 cells along its longer side (domains.jl). They are large (a few MB) and open on their own; they have no gallery. Publish them as the other figures (Figures/publish_figures.sh Domains).

title: Adding a dataset
text:
A dataset is one of three kinds, by how it is made from its sources:

a thematic dataset made by remapping (e.g. GHF, Velocity, SMB): fields from published maps, each source prepared once and remapped onto the grids of the domains. Most new datasets are of this kind. It is defined by <Dataset>/remap.toml.
a records dataset (e.g. IceCores, RSL): non-gridded data (time series, sites, profiles), whose prepared files are the products. It is defined by <Dataset>/records.toml.
a dataset with its own pipeline (Topo, Regions): processing beyond remapping (merging sources on the base grids, deriving fields), in a pipeline folder of its own.

All start from prepared sources, and end with the same steps to publish them (see Publishing a new dataset).


Each source has a folder named after it (<Author><Year>_<topic>, e.g. Lucazeau2019_ghf/) with a README.md (the data, where they come from, how to cite them, and their licence: check that it allows redistributing derived products before releasing them) and a prepare.jl (with its own Project.toml), which gets the original files through ../datamanifest.toml (with their DOI) and writes the prepared file(s) to $FESMDATA_PREPARED/<source>/. The form of a prepared file is described under Gridded data and Records format. The commands that make a dataset prepare its missing sources first.



A thematic dataset (e.g. GHF, geothermal heat flow) gathers the products of several sources on one theme, and is released like Topo, with its own versions (tags ghf-vX.Y.Z). It is defined by <Dataset>/remap.toml, one table per product:
[products.Lucazeau2019]                      # → <GRID>_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc
source = "Lucazeau2019_ghf"                  # source folder, with prepare.jl
file = "Lucazeau2019_GHF.nc"                 # prepared file of the source (or a list, see below)
variables = ["ghf", "ghf_sd"]                # optional, default all
grids = { Antarctica = 4, Greenland = 4, Global = 4 }   # by domain, see below
# method = "con"                             # optional, default "con"
# smooth = "auto"                            # optional, default "auto"
# release = false                            # optional: made, but not released
# figure = { variables = ["ghf"] }            # optional: its figure on the website
# fill = { variables = ["ux_srf", "uy_srf"], mask = "TOPO-BedMachine-v4" }   # optional: gaps over the ice (or "all") filled, see below
# precision = { ghf = 0.1 }                  # optional: precision of fields instead of the default, see below
# mask = { mask_ocn = 0.5 }                  # optional: integer masks of the coverage, see below


grids lists the domains (output folders) of the product, each with the grids it is made on; it is not made on other domains. For each domain:

a number: the minimum grid spacing in km, i.e. all standard grids of the domain not finer than this (on lon-lat grids, 111 km per degree of latitude); 0 means all. Finer grids are left out where a coarse source adds no information and its files would only be large; models that need finer grids can remap online. As a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the source spacing: 16 km and 0.5° (Global = 50) for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° (Global = 25) for sources at 0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most others.
a list of grid names: exactly these grids, e.g. Global = ["GLOBAL-T170"]. This also gives the grids made only on request, which no number selects: the Gaussian grids of the Global domain (gaussian in ../shared/domains.toml, e.g. GLOBAL-T170, the T170 grid of 512 x 256 used by VILMA).

For example, grids = { Antarctica = 16, Global = ["GLOBAL-T170"] } makes ANT-16KM, ANT-32KM and GLOBAL-T170.
Crops (Greenland, Laurentide, Eurasia, …) and nests are listed only for products their parent domain does not have (e.g. a Greenland-only source on Greenland): their grids lie on those of the parent, so fetch cuts a product of the parent to them on demand (see Nests and crops), and it is stored once.



fill fills the gaps of a source over the ice on each grid, after remapping (and the rotation of vectors): the cells of the fields variables with ice (H_ice > 0) in the Topo product mask on the same grid (<GRID>_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc in the same folder) but no source data (f_valid = 0) get the harmonic (Laplace) interpolation of the cells around them (laplace_fill of FesmUtils). With mask = "all", all the cells without source data are filled, e.g. outside the domain of a regional climate model, for fields used as model forcing over the whole grid. Gaps not connected to any data stay missing. Both components of a vector must be filled; the speed of a filled vector (the field with the standard name <x>_speed, for eastward_<x>_velocity) is the magnitude of the filled components there. Other fields (e.g. errors) stay missing in the gaps. The file has mask_fill (1: filled, 0: not; mask_fill_<field> when the fields differ) and the global attribute gap_fill. The Topo product must be made first (thematic datasets depend on Topo, and some on Regions).
fill can also be a list of tables, each with its method (each field in one of them): "harmonic" (the default, as above), "elevation_regression", for fields that depend on the surface elevation (e.g. the surface mass balance or temperature of a regional climate model, outside its ice mask or domain), or "elevation", for the surface elevation of the source itself (e.g. the orography of the regional climate model):
fill = [{ variables = ["pr", "sf"], mask = "all" },
        { method = "elevation_regression", variables = ["smb", "t2m", "T_srf"], mask = "all",
          cap = { smb = -91.7 } },       # optional: elevation, radius = 150.0, min_points = 20
        { method = "elevation", variables = ["z_srf"], mask = "all", gaps_of = "smb" }]   # optional: elevation, gaps_of
Each gap gets the linear regression of the field on the surface elevation, fitted over the cells with source data (f_valid > 0) within radius km (a disk; grown by radius / 2 until it holds at least min_points of them), at the elevation of the cell clamped to the range of the elevations of these cells (no extrapolation beyond the lowest and highest of them). The elevation, for the cells with data as for the gaps, is max(z_srf, 0) of the Topo product elevation on the same grid (default TOPO-BedMachine-v4): the surface elevation, never below sea level. Where the elevations of these cells hardly differ (variance below 1 m2), the gap gets their mean. Fields with extra dimensions are filled slice by slice (e.g. each month). cap gives upper bounds of the filled values, by field, in its units: of each value, or for a monthly field (extra dimension month of 12 only) of the annual mean, the months weighted by their mean length (February 28.25 days, as the -annual-mean products up to the leap days of their period), all months of a cell shifted down by the same amount, so that the seasonal cycle is kept. The log gives, for each field, the cells filled, the cell-slices whose radius was grown and the median slope. Vectors are filled by harmonic interpolation only.
"elevation" fills the gaps with the elevation of the regression itself, max(z_srf, 0) of the Topo product elevation (default TOPO-BedMachine-v4), not clamped (the clamp applies only within the regression). With gaps_of, it fills the cells (of mask) where that field has no source data, in any of its slices (e.g. any month), instead of the gaps of the variables themselves, and so also replaces source data there (marked by mask_fill). Filling the orography of the source where the surface mass balance is filled keeps it the reference elevation of the filled values, e.g. for an elevation correction of the surface mass balance in a model, also where the source has an orography of its own (e.g. 0 over its ocean).



file can be a list of prepared files of the source, each on its own grid, combined into one product. The files are meant to cover separate areas, e.g. the grounded and the floating ice of Antarctica on grids of their own (file = ["Smith2020_ANT.nc", "Smith2020_ANT_floating.nc"] in IceChange/remap.toml); they are not suited to alternative sources of the same quantity over the same area. Each file is remapped onto each grid as above; a field in one file only is taken as it is, and a field in several files (with the same units and extra dimensions) is the sum of their contributions, the value of each times the fraction of the cell it covers, divided by the sum of these fractions, with f_valid that sum. Where their remapped coverage overlaps (e.g. source grids offset from each other at a boundary) and the fractions add up to more than 1, f_valid is 1 and the value is the sum of the contributions, so that the total of each file is kept (for integer fields, the class of the file covering most of the cell). variables are taken from the files that have them, and fill applies to the combined fields. The global attributes of the files are joined (their distinct values), and remapped_from lists the files.



release = false makes a product locally but leaves it out of the releases, e.g. data obtained by personal communication whose redistribution the authors have not agreed to yet (say so in the README of the dataset).



precision sets the precision of some float fields instead of the default of their kind (see Precision and file sizes; ../shared/precision.jl), for fields that need more (or allow less): by field, an absolute tolerance in the units of the field (a number), a relative one ("x%") or "lossless", e.g. precision = { ghf = 0.1, smb = "1%", lat = "lossless" }. Each float field records its precision in the attributes precision and bitround_keepbits.



mask adds integer masks of the coverage of the source to the product, by name, each 1 where f_valid is at least its threshold and 0 elsewhere, with f_valid itself (on the same dimensions, e.g. a 3D ocean mask by depth). For a source missing on land and below the sea floor (ORAS5), mask = { mask_ocn = 0.5 } gives the ocean cells of each level that are mostly ocean. It needs one f_valid for all fields of the product.



An ensemble product is the mean or the standard deviation of other products of the dataset, its members, e.g. the models of a model intercomparison:
[products.PMIP3-lgm-mean]                    # → <GRID>_Paleoclimate-PMIP3-lgm-mean.nc
ensemble = ["PMIP3-CCSM4-lgm", "PMIP3-CNRM-CM5-lgm", ...]   # member products of the dataset
stat = "mean"                                # or "stdev"
grids = { Antarctica = 8, Global = 8 }       # members not made on some of these: intermediate there
# release = false, figure = { ... }, precision = { ... }   # optional, as above
It has no source, file, variables, method, smooth or fill: it is made on each grid from the files of its members on that grid (those missing are remapped first), after the other products. On a grid that is not one of a member’s own grids, the member is remapped as an intermediate file ($FESMDATA_WORK/remap/members/, full precision, not released), so that the statistics can be released on grids where the members are not, e.g. the 2 km grids of the mountain-glacier domains. Each of its fields is a field of any member (not f_valid, mask_fill or integer fields), with the same name, units and extra dimensions, and , ensemble mean or , ensemble standard deviation appended to its long name: in each cell, the mean or the standard deviation (population, divided by n, as cdo ensstd) of the members with a value there. n_<field> (a byte field) is the number of these members, e.g. 0 for a sea surface temperature over land. The global attributes of the members are joined, and ensemble_members lists them.
Domains are listed explicitly, so that the files of a release are fixed; each source must cover all its grids (one of its files, for a product of several files). The methods of remapping and smoothing (method, smooth) are described under Gridded data.



julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap GHF                          # all products, all grids
julia fesmdata.jl remap GHF Lucazeau2019 GLOBAL-0.5DEG    # one product, one grid
sbatch --job-name=remap-GHF Remap/jobs/remap_dataset.sbatch GHF   # Levante compute node
sbatch --job-name=remap-Sediment -p shared -c 64 --mem=58G -t 02:00:00 \
    Remap/jobs/remap_dataset.sbatch Sediment                  # small dataset, shared partition
The sources not prepared yet are prepared first. Existing files are kept unless --overwrite.
A new source of an existing thematic dataset is a new source folder and a new table [products.<Name>] in its remap.toml; add it to the table of products of the README of the dataset, run julia fesmdata.jl remap <Dataset> <Name>, and release a new version of the dataset.




A records dataset is defined by <Dataset>/records.toml, one table per product:
[products.Kindler2014]            # → IceCores-Kindler2014.nc (+ .txt)
source = "Kindler2014"            # source folder
file = "Kindler2014_NGRIP.nc"     # prepared file
# figure = { variable = "acc" }   # optional: the variable of its figure on the website
# text = false                    # optional: no text form (more than two axes, or too large)

[products.Rasmussen2014]          # → IceCores-Rasmussen2014-<part>.nc (+ .txt), one per part
source = "Rasmussen2014_GICC05"
files = { NGRIP = "Rasmussen2014_NGRIP.nc", GRIP = "Rasmussen2014_GRIP.nc" }   # part = prepared file
A product has either file or files: several files when its data do not share their axes (e.g. ice cores, each on its own time axis); part names have letters, digits and _ only.
The prepared files follow the Records format, with the provenance attributes (provenance_attrib(<tag>) of ../shared/provenance.jl). ../shared/records_prepare.jl has what most sources need: read_noaa and read_pangaea (the text tables of NOAA NCEI and PANGAEA), write_series (time series at sites, with the attributes) and aicc2023_age (AICC2023 ages of the Antarctic cores and NGRIP from their depths). Then
julia fesmdata.jl record IceCores                 # all products
julia fesmdata.jl record IceCores Kindler2014     # one product
prepares the missing sources, checks each prepared file against the form, copies it to $FESMDATA/Records/<Dataset>/<Dataset>-<Product>[-<part>].nc and writes its text form next to it (.txt; --overwrite to replace both). A records dataset is released on the domain Records (one package per dataset, Records_<Dataset>, and registry/Records/<Dataset>.toml); fesmdata.jl list, fetch and release work as for the gridded datasets.



A dataset that needs its own processing (merging sources, deriving fields) is a new pipeline folder, built like Topo and Regions, so that it can be released in the same way:

Folder <Dataset>/ with a README.md, Project.toml, common.jl, scripts/ (numbered steps) and jobs/.
Original datasets in ../datamanifest.toml, with their DOI, read through manifest() (../shared/manifest.jl).
common.jl includes ../shared/io.jl and ../shared/domains.jl, and sets const DATASET = "<name>" (lower case), the name of its provenance attributes and release tags (<name>-vX.Y.Z).
Output with write_fields(path, grid, fields; dataset=DATASET, ...), into $FESMDATA/<folder>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<NAME>[-<product>].nc on every grid of a domain (outdir(og) for each og in dom.grids). Add a sources attribute with the datamanifest.toml keys of the original datasets.
files.jl with the output file names and a function <name>_release_files(dom, og) giving the files of a release on a grid. It must need only ../shared/domains.jl (no other packages), since Publish reads it; add its functions to dataset_pipeline in ../Publish/release.jl (and include its files.jl there).




For every kind of dataset:

Release settings: add the dataset to ../Publish/datasets.toml (its release tag, title, README, keywords and description), and to a topic of the website ([_site] topics there).
README: write <Dataset>/README.md, which becomes its page on the website, in the form of the other datasets:

# <Dataset>: <title>, and 2-4 sentences: what it is, its kind, links to the Products and Domains pages;
## Products: a table of the products, with their source (and DOI), fields (units) and domains (for records: sites, variables, time);
notes on the fields and the method, in subsections where needed;
## Precision: the precision of its fields (see Precision and file sizes);
## Licences (or ## Sources and licences): the licence of each source;
## Making the dataset, last: the commands that make it, and how to add a source.

Figures: julia fesmdata.jl figures <Dataset> (see Website and figures, also for the options of figure).
Page: add docs/datasets/<name>.qmd, which includes the README, the downloads and the figures (as docs/datasets/ghf.qmd), and add it to the menu in docs/_quarto.yml.
Release (see Releasing): tag <tag>-vX.Y.Z, julia fesmdata.jl stamp <Dataset> at the tag, and julia fesmdata.jl release <Dataset>. The products page and the downloads of the dataset on the website are made from the registry.

With gaps_of, it fills the cells (of mask) where that field has no source data, in any of its slices (e.g. any month), instead of the gaps of the variables themselves, and so also replaces source data there (marked by mask_fill). file can be a list of prepared files of the source, each on its own grid, combined into one product. The files are meant to cover separate areas, e.g. the grounded and the floating ice of Antarctica on grids of their own (file = ["Smith2020_ANT.nc", "Smith2020_ANT_floating.nc"] in IceChange/remap.toml); they are not suited to alternative sources of the same quantity over the same area. Each file is remapped onto each grid as above; a field in one file only is taken as it is, and a field in several files (with the same units and extra dimensions) is the sum of their contributions, the value of each times the fraction of the cell it covers, divided by the sum of these fractions, with f_valid that sum. Where their remapped coverage overlaps (e.g. source grids offset from each other at a boundary) and the fractions add up to more than 1, f_valid is 1 and the value is the sum of the contributions, so that the total of each file is kept (for integer fields, the class of the file covering most of the cell). variables are taken from the files that have them, and fill applies to the combined fields. The global attributes of the files are joined (their distinct values), and remapped_from lists the files.



release = false makes a product locally but leaves it out of the releases, e.g. data obtained by personal communication whose redistribution the authors have not agreed to yet (say so in the README of the dataset).



precision sets the precision of some float fields instead of the default of their kind (see Precision and file sizes; ../shared/precision.jl), for fields that need more (or allow less): by field, an absolute tolerance in the units of the field (a number), a relative one ("x%") or "lossless", e.g. precision = { ghf = 0.1, smb = "1%", lat = "lossless" }. Each float field records its precision in the attributes precision and bitround_keepbits.



mask adds integer masks of the coverage of the source to the product, by name, each 1 where f_valid is at least its threshold and 0 elsewhere, with f_valid itself (on the same dimensions, e.g. a 3D ocean mask by depth). For a source missing on land and below the sea floor (ORAS5), mask = { mask_ocn = 0.5 } gives the ocean cells of each level that are mostly ocean. It needs one f_valid for all fields of the product.



An ensemble product is the mean or the standard deviation of other products of the dataset, its members, e.g. the models of a model intercomparison:
[products.PMIP3-lgm-mean]                    # → <GRID>_Paleoclimate-PMIP3-lgm-mean.nc
ensemble = ["PMIP3-CCSM4-lgm", "PMIP3-CNRM-CM5-lgm", ...]   # member products of the dataset
stat = "mean"                                # or "stdev"
grids = { Antarctica = 8, Global = 8 }       # members not made on some of these: intermediate there
# release = false, figure = { ... }, precision = { ... }   # optional, as above
It has no source, file, variables, method, smooth or fill: it is made on each grid from the files of its members on that grid (those missing are remapped first), after the other products. On a grid that is not one of a member’s own grids, the member is remapped as an intermediate file ($FESMDATA_WORK/remap/members/, full precision, not released), so that the statistics can be released on grids where the members are not, e.g. the 2 km grids of the mountain-glacier domains. Each of its fields is a field of any member (not f_valid, mask_fill or integer fields), with the same name, units and extra dimensions, and , ensemble mean or , ensemble standard deviation appended to its long name: in each cell, the mean or the standard deviation (population, divided by n, as cdo ensstd) of the members with a value there. n_<field> (a byte field) is the number of these members, e.g. 0 for a sea surface temperature over land. The global attributes of the members are joined, and ensemble_members lists them.
Domains are listed explicitly, so that the files of a release are fixed; each source must cover all its grids (one of its files, for a product of several files). The methods of remapping and smoothing (method, smooth) are described under Gridded data.



julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap GHF                          # all products, all grids
julia fesmdata.jl remap GHF Lucazeau2019 GLOBAL-0.5DEG    # one product, one grid
sbatch --job-name=remap-GHF Remap/jobs/remap_dataset.sbatch GHF   # Levante compute node
sbatch --job-name=remap-Sediment -p shared -c 64 --mem=58G -t 02:00:00 \
    Remap/jobs/remap_dataset.sbatch Sediment                  # small dataset, shared partition
The sources not prepared yet are prepared first. Existing files are kept unless --overwrite.
A new source of an existing thematic dataset is a new source folder and a new table [products.<Name>] in its remap.toml; add it to the table of products of the README of the dataset, run julia fesmdata.jl remap <Dataset> <Name>, and release a new version of the dataset.

title: Adding a dataset
text:
A records dataset is defined by <Dataset>/records.toml, one table per product:
[products.Kindler2014]            # → IceCores-Kindler2014.nc (+ .txt)
source = "Kindler2014"            # source folder
file = "Kindler2014_NGRIP.nc"     # prepared file
# figure = { variable = "acc" }   # optional: the variable of its figure on the website
# text = false                    # optional: no text form (more than two axes, or too large)

[products.Rasmussen2014]          # → IceCores-Rasmussen2014-<part>.nc (+ .txt), one per part
source = "Rasmussen2014_GICC05"
files = { NGRIP = "Rasmussen2014_NGRIP.nc", GRIP = "Rasmussen2014_GRIP.nc" }   # part = prepared file
A product has either file or files: several files when its data do not share their axes (e.g. ice cores, each on its own time axis); part names have letters, digits and _ only.
The prepared files follow the Records format, with the provenance attributes (provenance_attrib(<tag>) of ../shared/provenance.jl). ../shared/records_prepare.jl has what most sources need: read_noaa and read_pangaea (the text tables of NOAA NCEI and PANGAEA), write_series (time series at sites, with the attributes) and aicc2023_age (AICC2023 ages of the Antarctic cores and NGRIP from their depths). Then
julia fesmdata.jl record IceCores                 # all products
julia fesmdata.jl record IceCores Kindler2014     # one product
prepares the missing sources, checks each prepared file against the form, copies it to $FESMDATA/Records/<Dataset>/<Dataset>-<Product>[-<part>].nc and writes its text form next to it (.txt; --overwrite to replace both). A records dataset is released on the domain Records (one package per dataset, Records_<Dataset>, and registry/Records/<Dataset>.toml); fesmdata.jl list, fetch and release work as for the gridded datasets.

title: Adding a dataset
text:
A dataset that needs its own processing (merging sources, deriving fields) is a new pipeline folder, built like Topo and Regions, so that it can be released in the same way:

Folder <Dataset>/ with a README.md, Project.toml, common.jl, scripts/ (numbered steps) and jobs/.
Original datasets in ../datamanifest.toml, with their DOI, read through manifest() (../shared/manifest.jl).
common.jl includes ../shared/io.jl and ../shared/domains.jl, and sets const DATASET = "<name>" (lower case), the name of its provenance attributes and release tags (<name>-vX.Y.Z).
Output with write_fields(path, grid, fields; dataset=DATASET, ...), into $FESMDATA/<folder>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<NAME>[-<product>].nc on every grid of a domain (outdir(og) for each og in dom.grids). Add a sources attribute with the datamanifest.toml keys of the original datasets.
files.jl with the output file names and a function <name>_release_files(dom, og) giving the files of a release on a grid. It must need only ../shared/domains.jl (no other packages), since Publish reads it; add its functions to dataset_pipeline in ../Publish/release.jl (and include its files.jl there).

title: Adding a dataset
Overview and code
text:
How the FesmData datasets are made, and the code shared by all of them. The domains and grids as users see them are described on the Domains page.


Every dataset is made from the original sources, with each step in this repository:

Prepare: the folder of a source (e.g. Lucazeau2019_ghf/) has a prepare.jl that gets the original files (listed in ../datamanifest.toml) and writes them as a NetCDF file on their own grid, in a simple standard form, to $FESMDATA_PREPARED/<source>/.
Remap or pipeline: a thematic dataset (e.g. GHF/) groups the products of several sources in its remap.toml, and julia fesmdata.jl remap GHF puts the prepared files onto the grids of the domains, as $FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<Dataset>-<Product>.nc. Remapping is conservative (with smoothing where the grid is finer than the source), and handles extra dimensions (month, time, depth, …), integer fields (dominant class) and vectors (rotated to the grid axes); see Gridded data. Topo and Regions, which merge high-resolution sources on the base grid of each domain, have pipelines of their own (Topo/, Regions/). A records dataset (e.g. IceCores/) copies the prepared files as they are (records.toml, julia fesmdata.jl record IceCores).
Release: the products are uploaded to Helmholtz Codebase and listed in ../registry/ (see Releasing).

Adding a dataset describes the three kinds of datasets and how to add one.






Folder or file
Contents




fesmdata.jl
The command line of FesmData (julia fesmdata.jl help)


<Source>/
A source: README.md and prepare.jl (e.g. Lucazeau2019_ghf/)


<Dataset>/
A dataset: README.md and remap.toml (thematic) or records.toml (records)


Topo/, Regions/
The pipelines of Topo and Regions


Remap/
Remapping of prepared files and thematic datasets (fesmdata.jl remap)


Records/
Records datasets (fesmdata.jl record)


Publish/
Releases, downloads and the generated pages of the website (fesmdata.jl list, fetch, release, docs, …)


Figures/
Figures of the products for the website (fesmdata.jl figures)


registry/
The released products, one file per dataset and domain


docs/
The website (Quarto)


datamanifest.toml
The original datasets of all sources, with their DOIs


shared/domains.toml
The domains, their grids and output folders


shared/domains.jl
Domain(key): the base grid and all grids of a domain


shared/io.jl
NetCDF output (write_fields, write_grid_files) with the provenance attributes


shared/precision.jl
Default precision of the float fields by kind, and their bit rounding (see Precision and file sizes)


shared/provenance.jl
Repository paths, storage folders, provenance attributes


shared/manifest.jl
The original datasets (../datamanifest.toml)


shared/records_prepare.jl
For the prepare.jl of records: readers of NOAA and PANGAEA tables, write_series (time series at sites), AICC2023 ages


shared/ringgrid.jl
Gridding of equal-area points


shared/machines/
The environment of each machine (see Machines and storage)


maps/, grid/
Grid descriptions (cdo) of the v1 grids, and the tools that made them






Every NetCDF file written by a v2 pipeline has the global attributes source (this repository), fesmdata_version (git describe against the release tags of the dataset, e.g. topo-v2.0.0, with -dirty for uncommitted changes), fesmdata_commit and history (time, script and arguments) (provenance_attrib in provenance.jl). The products of Topo also have sources, the keys of their original datasets in ../datamanifest.toml, and remapped products the title, references, license and doi of their source.



The domains are defined in domains.toml (see Domains for what they are). A domain is a table:
[PYR]
folder = "Pyrenees"
proj = "+proj=tmerc +lat_0=0 +lon_0=3 +k=0.9996 +x_0=500000 +y_0=0 +a=6378137 +rf=298.257223563 +units=km"
xlim = [107.875, 487.625]     # first and last cell centres of the base grid (km)
ylim = [4639.875, 4811.625]
resolutions = [0.25, 0.5, 2]  # km; the first is the base grid
active = true                 # the default; false to leave it out of the releases

proj is a PROJ string with +units=km (false easting and northing in metres, as in PROJ).
Every resolution must be a whole multiple of the base resolution, and the extent a whole number of cells of each resolution (e.g. a multiple of the coarsest resolution), so that the grids are nested. Coarse grids extend half a coarse cell beyond the base grid, where their cells are means over the part the base grid covers.
Where a v1 grid exists in ../maps, take its extent, so that the v1 grids are reproduced (Topo step 1 reports which grids match).
folder must be unique among all domains, crops and nests.
elevation_precision (optional) is the tolerance (m) of the elevations and thicknesses on the grids of the domain, if not the default 0.01 m.

A lon-lat domain has type = "lonlat" and its resolutions in degrees, each dividing 180°; it needs no projection or extent. gaussian adds Gaussian grids, by spectral truncation and number of latitudes, made only for the products that name them:
[GLOBAL]
folder = "Global"
type = "lonlat"
resolutions = [0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5]
gaussian = { T170 = 256 }
A crop is a table below its domain, with its own folder and extent (on the cell centres of the base grid), and optionally only some of the resolutions of its domain. Its grids must lie on those of its domain at each resolution, i.e. its first cell centres must be cell centres of the domain grid at its coarsest resolution (checked when the domain is read), so that the products of the domain can be cut to them:
[NH.crops.LIS]
folder = "Laurentide"
xlim = [-4900, -36]
ylim = [-5400, 1576]

[PAT.crops.NPI]
folder = "NorthPatagonianIcefield"
xlim = [559.837171469987, 677.337171469987]
ylim = [4703.352314639904, 4872.352314639904]
resolutions = [0.25]
A nest is a table below its domain, with its own folder, extent and resolutions, on the projection of its domain (and active if its domain is, unless set). Its first and last cell centres at the resolutions it shares with its domain must be cell centres of the domain grids at these resolutions (checked when the domain is read); in the pipelines it is a domain like any other, named by its key (here SRG):
[PAT.nests.SRG]
folder = "SRG"
xlim = [583.087171469987, 634.837171469987]
ylim = [4811.102314639904, 4840.852314639904]
resolutions = [0.05, 0.1, 0.25]
An inactive domain (active = false) is left out of the releases, the website figures and the products made for all domains. Its grids and products are made when it is named (e.g. Topo/jobs/submit_domain.sh ALP); set it active to release it.
The grid files of each grid (grid_<GRID>.txt, <GRID>_grid.nc) are written by Topo step 1 (Topo/scripts/01_grids.jl), or by fesmdata.jl remap if they are missing (it downloads those released in Grids instead). They are released in the dataset Grids, once per grid.



Add the domain, crop or nest to domains.toml (above), or a new entry to resolutions. Then, for each dataset:

Topo: add the products of the domain to Topo/products.toml (see Topo), and run its steps for the domain, from step 1 (the grid files).
Regions: add the topography product for the zones of the domain to Regions/regions.toml ([zone] products), and basin sets if any to Regions/basins.toml (see Regions), and run its steps.
Thematic datasets (e.g. GHF): add the domain to the grids of its products in <Dataset>/remap.toml, and run julia fesmdata.jl remap <Dataset>. A nest or crop needs none: fetch crops those of its domain.

The domain is released with the next release of each dataset.

title: Your own gridded data
text:
Any gridded dataset (geothermal heat flow, basal melt, surface velocity, …) can be put on the FesmData grids in two steps:

Prepare: write the data as a NetCDF file on its own (native) grid, in a simple standard form. This is specific to each source and lives in the source’s folder.
Remap: one command puts that file onto any domains and grids, in the usual layout $FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/, including global lon-lat grids.

julia --project=Lucazeau2019_ghf Lucazeau2019_ghf/prepare.jl
julia fesmdata.jl remap $FESMDATA_PREPARED/Lucazeau2019_ghf/Lucazeau2019_GHF.nc Antarctica Global --name=GHF-Lucazeau2019
This writes, e.g., $FESMDATA/Antarctica/ANT-8KM/ANT-8KM_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc and $FESMDATA/Global/GLOBAL-1DEG/GLOBAL-1DEG_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc, on every grid of Antarctica and of the global lon-lat grids. The grid files of a grid, if missing, are downloaded from the dataset Grids when the grid is released there, else written.
To release it with FesmData, make it a product of a thematic dataset, e.g. GHF (see Adding a dataset). Non-gridded data (time series, sites, profiles) are not remapped: see Records format.


Make a folder for the source, named after it (e.g. Lucazeau2019_ghf/), with:

README.md: what the data are, where they come from, how to cite them, and their licence (check that it allows redistributing derived products before releasing them);
prepare.jl (with its own Project.toml): get the original files and write the prepared file(s) to $FESMDATA_PREPARED/<source folder>/ (in Julia: prepared_dir("<source folder>") from shared/provenance.jl).

A prepared file is a NetCDF file with:

a regular grid, given by 1D coordinate variables, either

lon, lat in degrees (units = "degrees_east", "degrees_north"): global or regional, with longitudes in -180:180 (preferred) or 0:360, in any order, and latitudes ascending or descending, evenly spaced or not (e.g. a Gaussian grid, with its cell edges from a CF bounds variable such as lat_bnds if there is one, else halfway between the latitudes); or
x, y in m or km, with the fields pointing to a grid-mapping variable (grid_mapping attribute) that holds a PROJ string in proj_params or proj4;

fields on that grid, each with units and long_name, and missing values as _FillValue or NaN. A field may have more dimensions than the grid (e.g. month, time, depth), each with a 1D coordinate variable; they are kept as they are. Variables off the grid are copied as they are, with their dimensions: on these dimensions (e.g. label(time)) or on dimensions of their own (e.g. an annual time series next to fields every 10 years, a section of the overturning streamfunction). Integer fields (e.g. masks, classes) stay integer, with flag_values and flag_meanings if they are classes. Vectors are given by their eastward and northward components, marked by the standard names eastward_<name> and northward_<name> (e.g. eastward_land_ice_surface_velocity), never by their components along the axes of a projected source grid;
optionally, fields given by region, one value per region of a Regions product (e.g. melt rates averaged over each drainage basin): a float variable on one dimension whose coordinate variable holds the region numbers, with units, long_name and the attribute regions, the Regions product (e.g. bmelt_basin(basin), regions = "BASINS-Zwally2012", basin = 1, …, 27). On each grid, every cell gets the value of its region, the field named as the dimension (basin) in <GRID>_<regions>.nc (Regions must be made first); the cells outside the regions (e.g. the open ocean beyond the shelf break, where the basins end) get the nearest region (FesmUtils extend_labels), so the field covers the whole grid and is constant over each region. They have no f_valid and are not filled or smoothed. A prepared file needs at least one field on its grid;
global attributes title, references, license and, where there is one, doi (copied to the remapped files).

Prepare the data at their own resolution: no smoothing or regridding, that is left to the remapping. Keep names and units simple (e.g. ghf in mW m-2).



julia fesmdata.jl remap <file.nc> <Domain> | <GRID> | all ... [options]

Targets are domains (e.g. Antarctica, all of its grids; Global, the global lon-lat grids), grids (e.g. GRL-4KM, GLOBAL-0.5DEG), or all. The names are listed under Domains.
--vars=a,b remaps only these fields (default: all fields of the file).
--name=NAME names the output <GRID>_<NAME>.nc (default: the file name). Use <Dataset>-<Source>, e.g. GHF-Lucazeau2019.
--method=con|bilinear (default con) and --smooth=auto|<km> (default auto), see below.
Existing files are kept unless --overwrite.

Methods. con (conservative) gives every cell the area-weighted mean of the source over the cell: it keeps means and totals, and is right for any grid coarser than the source. A source on the same projection as the grid, or a lon-lat source on a lon-lat grid, is remapped exactly; otherwise each cell is sampled at points spaced at most half the source spacing. bilinear interpolates the source at the cell centres. Fields with more dimensions are remapped one 2D slice at a time. Integer fields are remapped as classes, whatever the method: each cell gets the class that covers most of it (from the conservatively remapped area fraction of each class), or is missing where the source has no data. Vectors are remapped component by component and then rotated to the axes of a projected grid (attribute vector_component); on lon-lat grids they stay eastward and northward.
Smoothing. After remapping, the field can be smoothed with a Gaussian of standard deviation --smooth (km; 0 for none). With auto (the default), a source coarser than the grid that is remapped conservatively is smoothed with half the source spacing (e.g. about 28 km for a 0.5° source), the least that removes the steps between its cells; a source finer than the grid is not smoothed. Smoothing leaves out missing cells and does not spread data into them. The global attribute remap_method records what was done on each grid.
Each output file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by source data (f_valid_<field> per field when the fields have different coverage, with the extra dimensions of the field when its coverage differs between them, e.g. ocean data at depth). Cells without data are missing. Grids that the source does not cover at all are skipped, so a regional source (e.g. velocities of Greenland) can be remapped onto all. The grid files of each grid are written too if they are missing.
Run with threads for large grids: julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap ... (or set JULIA_NUM_THREADS).



The Global domain has global lon-lat grids at 0.1°, 0.25°, 0.5°, 1°, 2° and 5° (GLOBAL-0.1DEG, …), with cell edges at -180° and -90°. Global sources are best remapped onto these rather than released on their own grid, so that all global products share the same grids. Other domains, projected or lon-lat, can be added in shared/domains.toml (see Overview and code).




Files that are parts of one product along an extra dimension (e.g. a time series from yearly files, or a climatology): prepare them into one file first. (A product of a thematic dataset can combine several files in space only, see Several files.)
Projected grids described only by CF grid-mapping parameters or WKT (add a PROJ string as proj_params).

title: Velocity: ice surface velocity
text:
Surface velocity of the ice sheets from satellite observations, remapped onto the grids of the domains. Velocity is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in Velocity/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




Velocity-Joughin2018
Joughin et al. (2018): MEaSUREs multi-year Greenland velocity mosaic 1995-2015, 250 m (NSIDC-0670 v1), doi:10.5067/QUA5Q9SVMSJG
ux_srf, uy_srf (along the grid axes), uxy_srf (speed), ux_srf_err, uy_srf_err (m yr-1)
Greenland


Velocity-Rignot2011
Rignot et al. (2011): MEaSUREs InSAR-based Antarctic velocity 1995-2016, 450 m (NSIDC-0484 v2), doi:10.5067/D7GK8F5J8M8R
ux_srf, uy_srf (along the grid axes), uxy_srf (speed), ux_srf_err, uy_srf_err (m yr-1)
Antarctica


Velocity-Mouginot2019
Mouginot et al. (2019): MEaSUREs phase-based Antarctic velocity 1996-2018, 450 m (NSIDC-0754 v1), doi:10.5067/PZ3NJ5RXRH10
ux_srf, uy_srf (along the grid axes), uxy_srf (speed), ux_srf_err, uy_srf_err (m yr-1), mask_fill
Antarctica



The velocity components are remapped conservatively as eastward and northward components and then rotated to the axes of each grid. The speed uxy_srf is the remapped speed of the source (the mean speed in each cell, not the speed of the mean velocity). The errors are those of the source along the axes of its projection, which is that of the grids. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source.
In Velocity-Mouginot2019, the gaps of the source over the ice are filled on each grid: the cells with ice in TOPO-BedMachine-v4 (H_ice > 0) but no data (f_valid = 0) get ux_srf, uy_srf by harmonic (Laplace) interpolation of the cells around them, and uxy_srf is their magnitude there; the errors stay missing. These cells have mask_fill = 1.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): the velocities and their errors to 1% or 1 m yr-1, the larger; f_valid to 0.001. mask_fill is exact.

title: SMB: surface mass balance and surface climate
text:
Surface mass balance and surface climate of the ice sheets from regional climate models, remapped onto the grids of the domains. SMB is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in SMB/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




SMB-RACMO2.4p1-1981-2010, SMB-RACMO2.4p1-1991-2020, SMB-RACMO2.4p1-annual; annual means SMB-RACMO2.4p1-1981-2010-annual-mean, SMB-RACMO2.4p1-1991-2020-annual-mean
van Dalum et al. (2025): RACMO2.4p1 forced by ERA5, 11 km, doi:10.5194/tc-19-4061-2025, data doi:10.5281/zenodo.19255213
smb, pr, sf, runoff, melt, subl (kg m-2 yr-1), t2m, T_srf (K): monthly climatologies and their annual means, annual values 1979-2023; z_srf, f_ice, mask_land, mask_icesheet
Antarctica


SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1981-2010, SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1991-2020, SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1985-2014, SMB-RACMO2.3p2-annual; annual means SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1981-2010-annual-mean, SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1991-2020-annual-mean, SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1985-2014-annual-mean
van Wessem et al. (2018, 2023): RACMO2.3p2 forced by ERA5, 27 km, doi:10.5194/tc-12-1479-2018, data doi:10.5281/zenodo.7760491
smb, pr, sf, runoff, melt, subl (kg m-2 yr-1), t2m, T_srf (K): monthly climatologies and their annual means, annual values 1979-2022; z_srf, f_ice, mask_grounded. 1985-2014: reference climate of ISMIP7, filled over the whole grid (see below)
Antarctica


SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990, SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010, SMB-MARv3.14-1991-2020, SMB-MARv3.14-annual; annual means SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990-annual-mean, SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010-annual-mean, SMB-MARv3.14-1991-2020-annual-mean
Fettweis et al. (2017), Timmermans et al. (2026): MAR v3.14.3 forced by ERA5, 1 km, doi:10.5194/tc-11-1015-2017
smb, pr, sf, rf, melt, runoff (kg m-2 yr-1), t2m, T_srf (K): monthly climatologies and their annual means, annual values 1940-2025; z_srf, f_ice, mask
Greenland



All sources use the same names and units: fluxes in kg m-2 yr-1 (mm water equivalent per year), also for the months of a climatology, and temperatures in K. The -annual-mean products are the annual means (x, y) of the monthly climatologies, the months weighted by their mean length over the period. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and smoothed on grids finer than the source; the masks are remapped as classes.
SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1985-2014 (and its annual mean) is a reference climate for model forcing (the reference period of the ISMIP7 experiments), defined on the whole grid: smb is pr + subl off the glaciated surfaces (see vanWessem2023_racmo23), and smb, pr, sf, t2m, T_srf and z_srf are filled outside the RACMO domain (the corners of the grids) by harmonic interpolation (fill, mask = "all", marked by mask_fill).
SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1981-2010, SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990 and SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010 (and their annual means) are also defined on the whole grid, for model forcing, but filled where there are no source data (f_valid = 0, marked by mask_fill_<field>) as follows:

smb is defined on the ice only (RACMO: f_ice >= 0.1; MAR: its ice mask, see Fettweis2017_mar314, so that the cells at the ice margin are not mixed with the strongly negative values of MAR off the ice). Off the ice and outside the RCM domain (e.g. the ice caps of the Canadian Arctic on the GRL grids), it is the linear regression of smb on the surface elevation over the cells with data within 150 km (grown until there are 20), at the elevation of the cell (max(z_srf, 0) of TOPO-BedMachine-v4) clamped to the range of the elevations of these cells (no extrapolation), at most -91.7 kg m-2 yr-1 (-0.1 m yr-1 ice equivalent, with 917 kg m-3): a small negative surface mass balance off the ice, on land and ocean. In the monthly climatologies the bound applies to the annual mean (months weighted by their length), all months shifted by the same amount (fill, method = "elevation_regression", see Gap filling).
t2m and T_srf: the same regression on the elevation (a local lapse rate), without bound. They are missing only outside the RCM domain (RACMO: the corners of the grids; MAR: e.g. the Canadian Arctic), as the RCMs give them on land and ocean.
z_srf (the RCM orography): the elevation of the regression, max(z_srf, 0) of TOPO-BedMachine-v4, in every cell where smb is filled (method = "elevation", gaps_of = "smb"), also where the RCM has an orography of its own (e.g. 0 over the ocean of MAR, in the Canadian Arctic), so that it is the reference elevation of the filled smb (e.g. for an elevation correction in a model). Elsewhere it is the RCM orography, the elevation of the RCM t2m and T_srf where only smb is filled.
pr, sf (and rf for MAR, so that pr = sf + rf holds): harmonic interpolation. Off the ice, smb is not pr minus runoff or sublimation (which stay missing there), but the bound above.

runoff, melt and subl are not filled.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): smb, pr, sf, rf, runoff, melt and subl to 1%; t2m and T_srf to 0.01 K; z_srf to 0.01 m; f_ice and f_valid to 0.001. The masks are exact.

smb, pr, sf, runoff, melt, subl (kg m-2 yr-1), t2m, T_srf (K): monthly climatologies and their annual means, annual values 1979-2022; z_srf, f_ice, mask_grounded. 1985-2014: reference climate of ISMIP7, filled over the whole grid (see below)
Antarctica


SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990, SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010, SMB-MARv3.14-1991-2020, SMB-MARv3.14-annual; annual means SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990-annual-mean, SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010-annual-mean, SMB-MARv3.14-1991-2020-annual-mean
Fettweis et al. (2017), Timmermans et al. (2026): MAR v3.14.3 forced by ERA5, 1 km, doi:10.5194/tc-11-1015-2017
smb, pr, sf, rf, melt, runoff (kg m-2 yr-1), t2m, T_srf (K): monthly climatologies and their annual means, annual values 1940-2025; z_srf, f_ice, mask
Greenland



All sources use the same names and units: fluxes in kg m-2 yr-1 (mm water equivalent per year), also for the months of a climatology, and temperatures in K. The -annual-mean products are the annual means (x, y) of the monthly climatologies, the months weighted by their mean length over the period. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and smoothed on grids finer than the source; the masks are remapped as classes.
SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1985-2014 (and its annual mean) is a reference climate for model forcing (the reference period of the ISMIP7 experiments), defined on the whole grid: smb is pr + subl off the glaciated surfaces (see vanWessem2023_racmo23), and smb, pr, sf, t2m, T_srf and z_srf are filled outside the RACMO domain (the corners of the grids) by harmonic interpolation (fill, mask = "all", marked by mask_fill).
SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1981-2010, SMB-MARv3.14-1961-1990 and SMB-MARv3.14-1981-2010 (and their annual means) are also defined on the whole grid, for model forcing, but filled where there are no source data (f_valid = 0, marked by mask_fill_<field>) as follows:

smb is defined on the ice only (RACMO: f_ice >= 0.1; MAR: its ice mask, see Fettweis2017_mar314, so that the cells at the ice margin are not mixed with the strongly negative values of MAR off the ice). Off the ice and outside the RCM domain (e.g. the ice caps of the Canadian Arctic on the GRL grids), it is the linear regression of smb on the surface elevation over the cells with data within 150 km (grown until there are 20), at the elevation of the cell (max(z_srf, 0) of TOPO-BedMachine-v4) clamped to the range of the elevations of these cells (no extrapolation), at most -91.7 kg m-2 yr-1 (-0.1 m yr-1 ice equivalent, with 917 kg m-3): a small negative surface mass balance off the ice, on land and ocean. In the monthly climatologies the bound applies to the annual mean (months weighted by their length), all months shifted by the same amount (fill, method = "elevation_regression", see Gap filling).
t2m and T_srf: the same regression on the elevation (a local lapse rate), without bound. They are missing only outside the RCM domain (RACMO: the corners of the grids; MAR: e.g. the Canadian Arctic), as the RCMs give them on land and ocean.
z_srf (the RCM orography): the elevation of the regression, max(z_srf, 0) of TOPO-BedMachine-v4, in every cell where smb is filled (method = "elevation", gaps_of = "smb"), also where the RCM has an orography of its own (e.g. 0 over the ocean of MAR, in the Canadian Arctic), so that it is the reference elevation of the filled smb (e.g. for an elevation correction in a model). Elsewhere it is the RCM orography, the elevation of the RCM t2m and T_srf where only smb is filled.
pr, sf (and rf for MAR, so that pr = sf + rf holds): harmonic interpolation. Off the ice, smb is not pr minus runoff or sublimation (which stay missing there), but the bound above.

runoff, melt and subl are not filled.

title: SeaLevel: global sea level over glacial cycles
text:
Reconstructions of global (mean or eustatic) sea level over glacial cycles, some with the contributions of the ice sheets: stacks and regressions of benthic δ18O, inverse modelling of ice sheets, the Red Sea record, and the ice sheets of PaleoMIST 1.0. SeaLevel is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in SeaLevel/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/SeaLevel/SeaLevel-<product>[-<part>].nc, each with its text form (.txt). Relative sea level indicators at sites are in RSL.

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
Masks of geographic regions, of present-day land, continental shelf and open ocean, and of ice-sheet drainage basins, on every grid of every active domain (see Domains). Regions is made by a pipeline of its own, from the bed elevation of the Topo product of each domain; the Products page shows its versions on each domain.

Regions are a tree defined once, globally, in regions.toml, from standard datasets (countries and EEZs, IHO seas, oceans, HydroBASINS, IMBIE basins), so the same region has the same code in every domain. Each level of the tree covers the globe without gaps or overlaps.
Zones separate present-day land, the continental shelf (up to the shelf break) and the open ocean, from the bed elevation of the topography product.
Basins (basins.toml) are the drainage basins of the ice sheets, extended over the land and shelf of their region up to the shelf break.
Domains are masks of the nests and crops of a domain on all grids of its family.






Product
Source
Fields
Domains




REGIONS
Marine Regions (EEZ-land union, IHO Sea Areas, Global Oceans and Seas), HydroBASINS, IMBIE basins (NSIDC-0709); the bed elevation of Topo
region_1, region_2, region_3 (region codes), zone (0-3), dist_shelfbreak (km)
All


BASINS-Mouginot2019
Greenland glacier basins, 260 basins in 7 regions (Mouginot & Rignot, 2019, doi:10.7280/D1WT11)
basin, basin_mask, basin_group

BASINS-Zwally2012

basin, basin_mask, basin_group

BASINS-IMBIE2016, BASINS-IMBIE2016-refined
IMBIE 2016 and refined basins (Mouginot et al., 2017, NSIDC-0709 v2, doi:10.5067/AXE4121732AD)
basin, basin_mask, basin_group
Antarctica, with its crops and nests


BASINS-Schmidt2025
Regions of the freshwater fluxes of the ice sheets (Schmidt et al., 2025, doi:10.5281/zenodo.17386710): 7 Mouginot regions of Greenland, 18 IMBIE 2016 basins of Antarctica

basin, basin_mask
GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, NEGIS


BASINS-NEGIS
Northeast Greenland Ice Stream in three parts: centre and south from the surface speed (Joughin et al., 2018), north from NEGIS-v1
basin, basin_mask
GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, NEGIS


DOMAINS
Extents of the nests and crops (../shared/domains.toml)
domain_<KEY> (0/1), one per nest and crop
Domains with nests or crops, with their crops and nests



The files are <GRID>_REGIONS.nc, <GRID>_BASINS-<set>.nc and <GRID>_DOMAINS.nc. Regions, zones and basins are computed on the base grid of a domain (e.g. ANT-500M, GRL-PAL-500M, NH-2KM, PAT-250M, SRG-50M) and then mapped onto all other grids and crops, as for the topography; a nest (e.g. SRG in PAT) is computed on its own base grid. On each other grid, region codes, zones and basins are the class covering most of a cell, nested level by level (a cell’s region_3 lies within its region_2; basins within their group), and dist_shelfbreak is the cell mean.



A region is named by its path in the tree: “1.3.1” is subregion 1 of region 3 of region 1. Its code is the integer with two digits per level below the first: “1” = 1, “1.3” = 103, “1.3.1” = 10301. The files have one variable per level, region_1, region_2, region_3, each with the code of the deepest region at or above that level, so a cell without a subregion keeps the code of its region. The names of the codes are in the attributes flag_values and flag_meanings. Codes of ocean regions start at 51. Helpers for codes are in FesmUtils.jl (region_code, region_path, region_ancestor, in_region).







Level 2
Level 3




1.1 North America
1.1.1 Canadian Arctic Archipelago, 1.1.2 Hudson Bay and Strait, 1.1.3 Cordillera and Alaska


1.2 Western Eurasia
1.2.1 Barents-Kara, 1.2.2 British Isles, 1.2.3 Svalbard, 1.2.4 Fennoscandia


1.3 Greenland, 1.4 Asia, 1.5 Iceland, 1.6 Africa, 1.7 Latin America and the Caribbean, 1.8 Oceania



1.51 Arctic Ocean, 1.52 North Atlantic Ocean (with Baltic and Mediterranean), 1.53 North Pacific Ocean, 1.54 Indian Ocean, 1.55 South China and Eastern Archipelagic Seas



2.1 Antarctica (south of 60S)
2.1.1 West Antarctica, 2.1.2 East Antarctica, 2.1.3 Antarctic Peninsula


2.2 Latin America and the Caribbean, 2.3 Africa, 2.4 Asia, 2.5 Oceania, 2.51 South Atlantic, 2.52 South Pacific, 2.53 Indian Ocean, 2.54 South China and Eastern Archipelagic Seas




The rules of each region are documented in regions.toml. In short:

Continents are the countries and their EEZs grouped by UN M49 region; Greenland and Iceland come first; oceans (GOaS) take the rest. The high seas of the Davis Strait, which GOaS puts in the Arctic Ocean, are in the North Atlantic, with the rest of the high seas of the Labrador Sea. The high seas of the Norwegian and Greenland seas, a pocket enclosed by the EEZs of Norway, the Faroe Islands, Iceland and Greenland that GOaS also puts in the Arctic Ocean, are in Western Eurasia.
Russia is split between Western Eurasia and Asia at the divide between the rivers draining to the Kara and Laptev seas (HydroBASINS), and at sea at the boundary between the Kara and Laptev seas (IHO). Its EEZ in the Baltic and Black seas is in Western Eurasia.
The NA subregions follow HydroBASINS and IHO seas; Hudson Bay and Strait include only the coastal basins draining into them, not the large rivers, and all their islands. Cordillera and Alaska includes the EEZs of North America in the Pacific.
The Antarctic subregions are the IMBIE regions, extended to fill all of 2.1.
Cells of a region enclosed by its subregions but covered by none of them (where the coastlines of the sources do not match) get the nearest subregion.

The mountain-glacier domains lie within few regions of level 2: e.g. PYR in 1.2 Western Eurasia (land and EEZs of Spain, France and Andorra) and 1.52 North Atlantic Ocean (beyond the EEZs, if any), PAT and its nests in 2.2 Latin America and the Caribbean.



zone is 3 for present-day land (ice-free land and grounded ice), 2 for the continental shelf (including floating ice), 1 for open ocean within buffer (50 km) of the shelf break, and 0 for the open ocean beyond. dist_shelfbreak (km) is the distance to the shelf break, positive in the open ocean, so other buffers are a threshold on it.
The open ocean is the ice-free ocean connected to the abyss (deeper than z_abyss = -2000 m) through cells deeper than the shelf-break depth z_break (-500 m, -1000 m around Antarctica), after removing channels narrower than about 100 km (an opening of radius r_open = 50 km), which also smooths the shelf break. Deep troughs on the shelf that deepen towards the ice sheet are therefore shelf. The parameters are in regions.toml.
A domain without open ocean, where no ocean deeper than z_abyss lies within the domain (e.g. the mountain-glacier domains PYR and SRG), has only land and shelf, and dist_shelfbreak is -Inf everywhere (as noted in the comment attribute of the variable).



Each file has basin, basin_mask (1 within the original basins) and, for sets with groups (e.g. Mouginot regions, IMBIE regions, Zwally systems), basin_group. The islands in the ice shelves of IMBIE2016-refined keep their extent but are not extended, so the ice shelves around them go to the neighbouring grounded basins.
SanRafael is a single basin (1), the cells at least half covered by the glacier, not extended: the part of the SRG domain that evolves freely in yelmox, while the rest relaxes to the present-day state (in v1, regions = 1 of SRG-250M_REGIONS.nc). PYR has no basins.


The regions to which the freshwater fluxes of the ice sheets are attributed in the protocol of Schmidt et al. (2025) (GL_regions_3413.gpkg, AQ_regions_3031.gpkg of Zenodo record 17386710), so that their time series (see Schmidt2025_fwf) can be mapped onto the grids. basin is the region number of the time series (names in alphabetical order): Greenland 1-7 = CE, CW, NE, NO, NW, SE, SW; Antarctica 1-18 = A-Ap, Ap-B, …, K-A, grouped in basin_group by IMBIE region (East, Peninsula, West).
The polygons cover the ice sheets only (and not the ocean). In Greenland they are the Mouginot (2019) regions without their peripheral ice caps (ICE_CAPS_*, 59 000 km2), which go to the nearest region in the extension: the set is the same region as the groups of Mouginot2019 on 99.99% of the cells of the polygons and 98% after the extension. In Antarctica they are the IMBIE 2016 basins of NSIDC-0709 v2 (identical geometry), so the set is identical to IMBIE2016.
The basins are extended as the other sets (over land and shelf up to the shelf break), not as in the *_regions_*_flood.nc files of the record: these are the regions grown over the whole rectangle around the ice sheet at 1 km (GRASS r.grow, nearest region in straight line, over the open ocean and other land), and the Antarctic one is numbered in another order than the time series (A-Ap = 7, Ap-B = 11, …).



The NEGIS sets split the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream into three parts, to tune basal friction by part in yelmox: basin 1 centre (the trunk of 79N and Zachariae Isstrom down to the coast), 2 south (the trunk upstream), 3 north (the northern arm), 0 outside. They are not extended, so basin_mask is basin != 0, and have no groups (negis.jl).
NEGIS-v1 are the parts of yelmox v1 (basin_sub 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 of GRL-16KM_BASINS-nasa-negis-three.nc), drawn by hand by Ilaria Tabone (2024) on GRL-16KM. They cannot be rebuilt, so the 248 cells are kept in the repository (sources/negis_v1_GRL-16KM.csv). Each cell of the base grid takes the part of the GRL-16KM cell containing its centre, so GRL-16KM reproduces v1 exactly (checked by 06_negis.jl, 0 cells differ), and the other grids are the majority as for all basins.
NEGIS builds the centre and south parts from the present-day surface speed, the cell mean of the 250 m MEaSUREs velocity mosaic (NSIDC-0670 v1; Joughin et al., 2018) on the base grid. The stream is the cells of Zwally drainage system 2 with grounded ice (the topography of the zones) and a speed of at least 50 m/yr (30 m/yr south of the cut), connected to the cell nearest to (400, -1162) km in the trunk of 79N. This leaves out the separate fast cells of Storstrommen and L. Bistrup Brae. South is the stream south of the cut line y = -1140 - 0.3 x (km, GRL polar stereographic), centre the rest. The north part of v1 follows a palaeo ice stream that shut down in the Holocene (Franke et al., 2022) and is slow today (4-50 m/yr), so neither a lower speed threshold nor a band along the present flow reproduces it (IoU of the north part 0.50 and 0.73 at best). Franke et al. publish only the radar data (PANGAEA), not an outline, so the north part is that of NEGIS-v1, and replaces the others where they overlap. The parameters are in basins.toml ([basins.negis]).

<GRID>_DOMAINS.nc locates the nests and crops of a domain family (a domain with all its nests and crops) on every grid of the family, e.g. NPI, SPI, SRG, GCN, CDI, SAR and SCH on the grids of PAT, of its crops and of its nests. domain_<KEY> (int8) is 1 where the cell centre lies within the extent of nest or crop KEY, the cell edges of its base grid (that of its domain for a crop), and 0 elsewhere; one variable per nest or crop, as they may overlap (SRG lies in NPI). Its attributes give the folder (long_name), kind (nest or crop), parent (key) and extent (x0, x1, y0, y1, km). Only active nests and crops are included, and domains without any (e.g. PYR) have no file. The masks are computed on each grid from the cell centres (07_domains.jl).



Region codes, zones and basins are integers and exact. dist_shelfbreak (km) is rounded on output to 3 significant digits (see Precision and file sizes); the intermediate files on the base grid (steps 1-3) are not rounded.

A region is an entry of regions.toml, with its path, name and rules:
[[region]]
path = "1.2.3"
name = "Svalbard"
rules = [{ source = "eez_land", field = "territory1", values = ["Svalbard"] }]
A region covers the union of its rules, within its parent; siblings are applied in the order of the file, so a cell taken by an earlier sibling stays with it. Cells of a region that none of its subregions covers keep the code of the region, unless its subregions enclose them. A rule selects features of a polygon source (eez_land, iho, goas, hydrobasins, imbie) by the values of a field, or a lon/lat box, and can be limited within or without other rules (see the header of regions.toml). A region with fill = true gives its cells outside all its subregions to the nearest subregion. Ocean regions are numbered from 51. Changing the tree changes the codes of all domains, so it is a new release of Regions; then run steps 1 and 4 (and 5) for every domain.
A basin set is an entry of basins.toml: its name, domains, the region it is extended in (up to the shelf break), its polygon source, and the attribute identifying the basins (id_field), optionally a grouping (group_field), selected features, or basins that are not extended (no_extension); see the header of basins.toml. Then run steps 3-5 for its domains (03_basins.jl <DOMAIN> <SET>, 04_grids.jl <DOMAIN> <SET>). Its files are released with the next release of Regions.
A polygon source is an entry of ../datamanifest.toml (with its DOI), a branch in _read_source and in manifest_keys in sources.jl (the polygons in lon/lat as Shapes, with their attributes).
A domain: define it in ../shared/domains.toml (see Overview and code), make its topography (Topo), and add the topography product of its zones to [zone] products in regions.toml (and its shelf-break depth z_break if its region needs another one). Add it to the domains of its basin sets, if any, and run all steps (jobs/submit_domain.sh <DOMAIN>). The region tree is global, so a new domain needs no new regions.

The regions, zones and basins are read with NCDatasets.jl; FesmUtils.jl has the functions for the region codes. All examples below are run as shown, in order, to make their maps.
using NCDatasets, FesmUtils

dir = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "North", "NH-16KM")
ds = NCDataset(joinpath(dir, "NH-16KM_REGIONS.nc"))



region_1, region_2 and region_3 hold the codes of the levels of the tree. A cell without a subregion keeps the code of its region: the cells of North America (1.1) outside its three subregions keep code 101 in region_3. The names of the codes are in the attributes of each variable.
region_1 = ds["region_1"][:, :]
region_2 = ds["region_2"][:, :]
region_3 = ds["region_3"][:, :]

attrib = ds["region_3"].attrib
region_names = Dict(zip(attrib["flag_values"], split(attrib["flag_meanings"])))
println(region_names[region_code("1.1.2")])
Hudson_Bay_and_Strait



The three levels of the regions on NH-16KM, labelled by path and name.





A code has two digits per level below the first, so the path, level and ancestors of a region follow from its code. Ocean regions are numbered from 51.
@show region_code("1.1.2")
@show region_path(10102)
@show region_level(10102)
@show region_ancestor(10102, 2)
@show region_code("1.52");
region_code("1.1.2") = 10102
region_path(10102) = "1.1.2"
region_level(10102) = 3
region_ancestor(10102, 2) = 101
region_code("1.52") = 152



in_region selects a region together with all its subregions. Comparing the codes of a level with == selects only the cells of the region that are in none of its subregions.
north_america = in_region(region_3, region_code("1.1"))   # with 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3
rest = region_3 .== region_code("1.1")                    # only the cells in none of them



North America selected with in_region (left) and with == (right) on NH-16KM.





zone separates the open ocean (0), the open ocean within 50 km of the shelf break (1), the continental shelf (2) and land (3); dist_shelfbreak is the distance to the shelf break (km, positive in the open ocean), for other widths of the band along it. Combined with the regions, they give e.g. the shelf of a region.
zone = ds["zone"][:, :]
dist = ds["dist_shelfbreak"][:, :]

shelf = in_region(region_3, region_code("1.2")) .& (zone .== 2)   # shelf of Western Eurasia
band = 0 .< dist .< 200                                           # open ocean within 200 km



Zones, distance to the shelf break and their combinations on NH-16KM.





A basin set has the basins (basin), extended over the land and shelf of their region up to the shelf break, their groups (basin_group, if the set has them) and the original extent of the basins (basin_mask).
grl = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "GreenlandPaleo", "GRL-PAL-16KM")
bs = NCDataset(joinpath(grl, "GRL-PAL-16KM_BASINS-Zwally2012.nc"))

basin = bs["basin"][:, :]
group = bs["basin_group"][:, :]
original = ifelse.(bs["basin_mask"][:, :] .== 1, basin, missing)   # before the extension



The Zwally2012 basins of Greenland on GRL-PAL-16KM: basins, their groups (major drainage systems) and their original extent.





The tree is global, so a region has the same code on all domains and grids.
greenland = map(["North/NH-16KM", "GreenlandPaleo/GRL-PAL-16KM"]) do g
    file = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], g, basename(g) * "_REGIONS.nc")
    NCDataset(d -> in_region(d["region_2"][:, :], region_code("1.3")), file)
end



Region 1.3 Greenland (its land and EEZ) on NH-16KM and GRL-PAL-16KM.





The same files on Antarctica: the levels of the tree of the ice sheet, its ice shelves and the Southern Ocean.
ant = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "Antarctica", "ANT-16KM")
da = NCDataset(joinpath(ant, "ANT-16KM_REGIONS.nc"))
ant_regions = [da["region_$l"][:, :] for l in 1:3]



The three levels of the regions on ANT-16KM, labelled by path and name.





The zones of Antarctica and one of its basin sets, IMBIE2016 (the others are IMBIE2016-refined, Zwally2012 and Schmidt2025).
ant_zone = da["zone"][:, :]
ab = NCDataset(joinpath(ant, "ANT-16KM_BASINS-IMBIE2016.nc"))
ant_basin = ab["basin"][:, :]



Zones and the IMBIE2016 basins on ANT-16KM.
