The files are <GRID>_REGIONS.nc, <GRID>_BASINS-<set>.nc and <GRID>_DOMAINS.nc. Regions, zones and basins are computed on the base grid of a domain (e.g. ANT-500M, GRL-PAL-500M, NH-2KM, PAT-250M, SRG-50M) and then mapped onto all other grids and crops, as for the topography; a nest (e.g. SRG in PAT) is computed on its own base grid. On each other grid, region codes, zones and basins are the class covering most of a cell, nested level by level (a cell’s region_3 lies within its region_2; basins within their group), and dist_shelfbreak is the cell mean.

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
A region is named by its path in the tree: “1.3.1” is subregion 1 of region 3 of region 1. Its code is the integer with two digits per level below the first: “1” = 1, “1.3” = 103, “1.3.1” = 10301. The files have one variable per level, region_1, region_2, region_3, each with the code of the deepest region at or above that level, so a cell without a subregion keeps the code of its region. The names of the codes are in the attributes flag_values and flag_meanings. Codes of ocean regions start at 51. Helpers for codes are in FesmUtils.jl (region_code, region_path, region_ancestor, in_region).







Level 2
Level 3




1.1 North America
1.1.1 Canadian Arctic Archipelago, 1.1.2 Hudson Bay and Strait, 1.1.3 Cordillera and Alaska


1.2 Western Eurasia
1.2.1 Barents-Kara, 1.2.2 British Isles, 1.2.3 Svalbard, 1.2.4 Fennoscandia


1.3 Greenland, 1.4 Asia, 1.5 Iceland, 1.6 Africa, 1.7 Latin America and the Caribbean, 1.8 Oceania



1.51 Arctic Ocean, 1.52 North Atlantic Ocean (with Baltic and Mediterranean), 1.53 North Pacific Ocean, 1.54 Indian Ocean, 1.55 South China and Eastern Archipelagic Seas



2.1 Antarctica (south of 60S)
2.1.1 West Antarctica, 2.1.2 East Antarctica, 2.1.3 Antarctic Peninsula


2.2 Latin America and the Caribbean, 2.3 Africa, 2.4 Asia, 2.5 Oceania, 2.51 South Atlantic, 2.52 South Pacific, 2.53 Indian Ocean, 2.54 South China and Eastern Archipelagic Seas




The rules of each region are documented in regions.toml. In short:

Continents are the countries and their EEZs grouped by UN M49 region; Greenland and Iceland come first; oceans (GOaS) take the rest. The high seas of the Davis Strait, which GOaS puts in the Arctic Ocean, are in the North Atlantic, with the rest of the high seas of the Labrador Sea. The high seas of the Norwegian and Greenland seas, a pocket enclosed by the EEZs of Norway, the Faroe Islands, Iceland and Greenland that GOaS also puts in the Arctic Ocean, are in Western Eurasia.
Russia is split between Western Eurasia and Asia at the divide between the rivers draining to the Kara and Laptev seas (HydroBASINS), and at sea at the boundary between the Kara and Laptev seas (IHO). Its EEZ in the Baltic and Black seas is in Western Eurasia.
The NA subregions follow HydroBASINS and IHO seas; Hudson Bay and Strait include only the coastal basins draining into them, not the large rivers, and all their islands. Cordillera and Alaska includes the EEZs of North America in the Pacific.
The Antarctic subregions are the IMBIE regions, extended to fill all of 2.1.
Cells of a region enclosed by its subregions but covered by none of them (where the coastlines of the sources do not match) get the nearest subregion.

The mountain-glacier domains lie within few regions of level 2: e.g. PYR in 1.2 Western Eurasia (land and EEZs of Spain, France and Andorra) and 1.52 North Atlantic Ocean (beyond the EEZs, if any), PAT and its nests in 2.2 Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
zone is 3 for present-day land (ice-free land and grounded ice), 2 for the continental shelf (including floating ice), 1 for open ocean within buffer (50 km) of the shelf break, and 0 for the open ocean beyond. dist_shelfbreak (km) is the distance to the shelf break, positive in the open ocean, so other buffers are a threshold on it.
The open ocean is the ice-free ocean connected to the abyss (deeper than z_abyss = -2000 m) through cells deeper than the shelf-break depth z_break (-500 m, -1000 m around Antarctica), after removing channels narrower than about 100 km (an opening of radius r_open = 50 km), which also smooths the shelf break. Deep troughs on the shelf that deepen towards the ice sheet are therefore shelf. The parameters are in regions.toml.
A domain without open ocean, where no ocean deeper than z_abyss lies within the domain (e.g. the mountain-glacier domains PYR and SRG), has only land and shelf, and dist_shelfbreak is -Inf everywhere (as noted in the comment attribute of the variable).

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
Each file has basin, basin_mask (1 within the original basins) and, for sets with groups (e.g. Mouginot regions, IMBIE regions, Zwally systems), basin_group. The islands in the ice shelves of IMBIE2016-refined keep their extent but are not extended, so the ice shelves around them go to the neighbouring grounded basins.
SanRafael is a single basin (1), the cells at least half covered by the glacier, not extended: the part of the SRG domain that evolves freely in yelmox, while the rest relaxes to the present-day state (in v1, regions = 1 of SRG-250M_REGIONS.nc). PYR has no basins.


The regions to which the freshwater fluxes of the ice sheets are attributed in the protocol of Schmidt et al. (2025) (GL_regions_3413.gpkg, AQ_regions_3031.gpkg of Zenodo record 17386710), so that their time series (see Schmidt2025_fwf) can be mapped onto the grids. basin is the region number of the time series (names in alphabetical order): Greenland 1-7 = CE, CW, NE, NO, NW, SE, SW; Antarctica 1-18 = A-Ap, Ap-B, …, K-A, grouped in basin_group by IMBIE region (East, Peninsula, West).
The polygons cover the ice sheets only (and not the ocean). In Greenland they are the Mouginot (2019) regions without their peripheral ice caps (ICE_CAPS_*, 59 000 km2), which go to the nearest region in the extension: the set is the same region as the groups of Mouginot2019 on 99.99% of the cells of the polygons and 98% after the extension. In Antarctica they are the IMBIE 2016 basins of NSIDC-0709 v2 (identical geometry), so the set is identical to IMBIE2016.
The basins are extended as the other sets (over land and shelf up to the shelf break), not as in the *_regions_*_flood.nc files of the record: these are the regions grown over the whole rectangle around the ice sheet at 1 km (GRASS r.grow, nearest region in straight line, over the open ocean and other land), and the Antarctic one is numbered in another order than the time series (A-Ap = 7, Ap-B = 11, …).



The NEGIS sets split the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream into three parts, to tune basal friction by part in yelmox: basin 1 centre (the trunk of 79N and Zachariae Isstrom down to the coast), 2 south (the trunk upstream), 3 north (the northern arm), 0 outside. They are not extended, so basin_mask is basin != 0, and have no groups (negis.jl).
NEGIS-v1 are the parts of yelmox v1 (basin_sub 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 of GRL-16KM_BASINS-nasa-negis-three.nc), drawn by hand by Ilaria Tabone (2024) on GRL-16KM. They cannot be rebuilt, so the 248 cells are kept in the repository (sources/negis_v1_GRL-16KM.csv). Each cell of the base grid takes the part of the GRL-16KM cell containing its centre, so GRL-16KM reproduces v1 exactly (checked by 06_negis.jl, 0 cells differ), and the other grids are the majority as for all basins.
NEGIS builds the centre and south parts from the present-day surface speed, the cell mean of the 250 m MEaSUREs velocity mosaic (NSIDC-0670 v1; Joughin et al., 2018) on the base grid. The stream is the cells of Zwally drainage system 2 with grounded ice (the topography of the zones) and a speed of at least 50 m/yr (30 m/yr south of the cut), connected to the cell nearest to (400, -1162) km in the trunk of 79N. This leaves out the separate fast cells of Storstrommen and L. Bistrup Brae. South is the stream south of the cut line y = -1140 - 0.3 x (km, GRL polar stereographic), centre the rest. The north part of v1 follows a palaeo ice stream that shut down in the Holocene (Franke et al., 2022) and is slow today (4-50 m/yr), so neither a lower speed threshold nor a band along the present flow reproduces it (IoU of the north part 0.50 and 0.73 at best). Franke et al. publish only the radar data (PANGAEA), not an outline, so the north part is that of NEGIS-v1, and replaces the others where they overlap. The parameters are in basins.toml ([basins.negis]).
The parameters give the best match of the v1 parts on GRL-16KM, among cut lines, thresholds of the south part of 20-50 m/yr, and other splits (06_negis.jl):

The whole stream at 50 m/yr matches the single v1 NEGIS basin (basin 9 of GRL-16KM_BASINS-nasa-negis.nc) with IoU 0.88. The v1 centre also has a few isolated cells near Storstrommen, left out here. A cut at a surface elevation of 1450 m instead of the line gives IoU 0.74 (centre) and 0.79 (south), and a cut at a distance along the stream from the grounding line of 79N (200 km) 0.68 and 0.63. The Mouginot basins of 79N, Zachariae Isstrom and Storstrommen are far broader than the stream (IoU 0.23).

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text: <GRID>_DOMAINS.nc locates the nests and crops of a domain family (a domain with all its nests and crops) on every grid of the family, e.g. NPI, SPI, SRG, GCN, CDI, SAR and SCH on the grids of PAT, of its crops and of its nests. domain_<KEY> (int8) is 1 where the cell centre lies within the extent of nest or crop KEY, the cell edges of its base grid (that of its domain for a crop), and 0 elsewhere; one variable per nest or crop, as they may overlap (SRG lies in NPI). Its attributes give the folder (long_name), kind (nest or crop), parent (key) and extent (x0, x1, y0, y1, km). Only active nests and crops are included, and domains without any (e.g. PYR) have no file. The masks are computed on each grid from the cell centres (07_domains.jl).

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text: Region codes, zones and basins are integers and exact. dist_shelfbreak (km) is rounded on output to 3 significant digits (see Precision and file sizes); the intermediate files on the base grid (steps 1-3) are not rounded.

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
The machine environment is set up as described under Machines and storage.









Location
Contents




$FESMDATA_SOURCES
Original datasets (see ../datamanifest.toml)


$FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/
Output: <GRID>_REGIONS.nc, <GRID>_BASINS-<set>.nc, <GRID>_DOMAINS.nc


$FESMDATA_WORK/regions/
Intermediate files (base grids) and check plots






All commands are run from the FesmData root after sourcing the machine environment. Each step can be submitted as a job on a Levante compute node:
sbatch --job-name=<name> Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch <script> <args...>
and Regions/jobs/submit_domain.sh DOMAIN [FIRST_STEP] submits steps 1-5 as a chain of jobs, and step 7. The topography product of the domain (Topo, step 3) is needed from step 2.


The datasets are listed and downloaded with the Topo script (on a login node):
julia --project=Topo Topo/scripts/00_sources.jl --download
The Marine Regions layers (EEZ-land union v4, IHO Sea Areas v3, GOaS v1) are fetched from its WFS server, HydroBASINS, the Zwally drainage systems and the ISO 3166/M49 table directly. Two need a manual download into the folder printed by the script:

Mouginot & Rignot (2019) basins: the Greenland_Basins_PS_v1.4.2.* files from Dryad.
NSIDC-0709 v2 (NASA Earthdata login, see Topo): the .shp, .shx, .dbf and .prj files of Basins_IMBIE_Antarctica_v02 and Basins_Antarctica_v02, from the uri in ../datamanifest.toml.
NSIDC-0670 v1 (NASA Earthdata login): greenland_vel_mosaic250_vx_v1.tif and greenland_vel_mosaic250_vy_v1.tif (NEGIS), from the uri in ../datamanifest.toml.




sbatch --job-name=regions-NH Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 01_regions.jl NH
Writes region_1-region_3 on the base grid. The job log lists the cells of each region, and the cells that were filled with the nearest region.



sbatch --job-name=zone-NH Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 02_zone.jl NH



sbatch --job-name=basins-ANT Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 03_basins.jl ANT [SET]
NEGIS reads the grounded ice of the topography of the zones (step 2).



sbatch --job-name=grids-all-NH Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 04_grids.jl NH [SET]
With SET, only the files of that basin set are written.



sbatch --job-name=plots-NH Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 05_plots.jl NH [GRID]
Writes maps of the regions, zones and basins to $FESMDATA_WORK/regions/plots/.
The NEGIS sets are checked against v1 on GRL-16KM (cells and IoU of each part, and a map, $FESMDATA_WORK/regions/plots/GRL-16KM_negis.png):
sbatch --job-name=negis Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 06_negis.jl \
    /work/ba1442/ice_data/Greenland/GRL-16KM/GRL-16KM_BASINS-nasa-negis-three.nc
The v1 file is optional; with it, the script checks that NEGIS-v1 reproduces it.



sbatch --job-name=domains-PAT Regions/jobs/run_step.sbatch 07_domains.jl PAT
Writes <GRID>_DOMAINS.nc on all grids of the domain and its crops (run it for each domain and nest of a family). Needs no other step; rerun it for the whole family when a nest or crop is added or changed.




A region is an entry of regions.toml, with its path, name and rules:
[[region]]
path = "1.2.3"
name = "Svalbard"
rules = [{ source = "eez_land", field = "territory1", values = ["Svalbard"] }]
A region covers the union of its rules, within its parent; siblings are applied in the order of the file, so a cell taken by an earlier sibling stays with it. Cells of a region that none of its subregions covers keep the code of the region, unless its subregions enclose them. A rule selects features of a polygon source (eez_land, iho, goas, hydrobasins, imbie) by the values of a field, or a lon/lat box, and can be limited within or without other rules (see the header of regions.toml). A region with fill = true gives its cells outside all its subregions to the nearest subregion. Ocean regions are numbered from 51. Changing the tree changes the codes of all domains, so it is a new release of Regions; then run steps 1 and 4 (and 5) for every domain.
A basin set is an entry of basins.toml: its name, domains, the region it is extended in (up to the shelf break), its polygon source, and the attribute identifying the basins (id_field), optionally a grouping (group_field), selected features, or basins that are not extended (no_extension); see the header of basins.toml. Then run steps 3-5 for its domains (03_basins.jl <DOMAIN> <SET>, 04_grids.jl <DOMAIN> <SET>). Its files are released with the next release of Regions.
A polygon source is an entry of ../datamanifest.toml (with its DOI), a branch in _read_source and in manifest_keys in sources.jl (the polygons in lon/lat as Shapes, with their attributes).
A domain: define it in ../shared/domains.toml (see Overview and code), make its topography (Topo), and add the topography product of its zones to [zone] products in regions.toml (and its shelf-break depth z_break if its region needs another one). Add it to the domains of its basin sets, if any, and run all steps (jobs/submit_domain.sh <DOMAIN>). The region tree is global, so a new domain needs no new regions.

title: Regions: region masks, zones and basins
text:
The regions, zones and basins are read with NCDatasets.jl; FesmUtils.jl has the functions for the region codes. All examples below are run as shown, in order, to make their maps.
using NCDatasets, FesmUtils

dir = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "North", "NH-16KM")
ds = NCDataset(joinpath(dir, "NH-16KM_REGIONS.nc"))



region_1, region_2 and region_3 hold the codes of the levels of the tree. A cell without a subregion keeps the code of its region: the cells of North America (1.1) outside its three subregions keep code 101 in region_3. The names of the codes are in the attributes of each variable.
region_1 = ds["region_1"][:, :]
region_2 = ds["region_2"][:, :]
region_3 = ds["region_3"][:, :]

attrib = ds["region_3"].attrib
region_names = Dict(zip(attrib["flag_values"], split(attrib["flag_meanings"])))
println(region_names[region_code("1.1.2")])
Hudson_Bay_and_Strait



The three levels of the regions on NH-16KM, labelled by path and name.





A code has two digits per level below the first, so the path, level and ancestors of a region follow from its code. Ocean regions are numbered from 51.
@show region_code("1.1.2")
@show region_path(10102)
@show region_level(10102)
@show region_ancestor(10102, 2)
@show region_code("1.52");
region_code("1.1.2") = 10102
region_path(10102) = "1.1.2"
region_level(10102) = 3
region_ancestor(10102, 2) = 101
region_code("1.52") = 152



in_region selects a region together with all its subregions. Comparing the codes of a level with == selects only the cells of the region that are in none of its subregions.
north_america = in_region(region_3, region_code("1.1"))   # with 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3
rest = region_3 .== region_code("1.1")                    # only the cells in none of them



North America selected with in_region (left) and with == (right) on NH-16KM.





zone separates the open ocean (0), the open ocean within 50 km of the shelf break (1), the continental shelf (2) and land (3); dist_shelfbreak is the distance to the shelf break (km, positive in the open ocean), for other widths of the band along it. Combined with the regions, they give e.g. the shelf of a region.
zone = ds["zone"][:, :]
dist = ds["dist_shelfbreak"][:, :]

shelf = in_region(region_3, region_code("1.2")) .& (zone .== 2)   # shelf of Western Eurasia
band = 0 .< dist .< 200                                           # open ocean within 200 km



Zones, distance to the shelf break and their combinations on NH-16KM.





A basin set has the basins (basin), extended over the land and shelf of their region up to the shelf break, their groups (basin_group, if the set has them) and the original extent of the basins (basin_mask).
grl = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "GreenlandPaleo", "GRL-PAL-16KM")
bs = NCDataset(joinpath(grl, "GRL-PAL-16KM_BASINS-Zwally2012.nc"))

basin = bs["basin"][:, :]
group = bs["basin_group"][:, :]
original = ifelse.(bs["basin_mask"][:, :] .== 1, basin, missing)   # before the extension



The Zwally2012 basins of Greenland on GRL-PAL-16KM: basins, their groups (major drainage systems) and their original extent.





The tree is global, so a region has the same code on all domains and grids.
greenland = map(["North/NH-16KM", "GreenlandPaleo/GRL-PAL-16KM"]) do g
    file = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], g, basename(g) * "_REGIONS.nc")
    NCDataset(d -> in_region(d["region_2"][:, :], region_code("1.3")), file)
end



Region 1.3 Greenland (its land and EEZ) on NH-16KM and GRL-PAL-16KM.





The same files on Antarctica: the levels of the tree of the ice sheet, its ice shelves and the Southern Ocean.
ant = joinpath(ENV["FESMDATA"], "Antarctica", "ANT-16KM")
da = NCDataset(joinpath(ant, "ANT-16KM_REGIONS.nc"))
ant_regions = [da["region_$l"][:, :] for l in 1:3]



The three levels of the regions on ANT-16KM, labelled by path and name.





The zones of Antarctica and one of its basin sets, IMBIE2016 (the others are IMBIE2016-refined, Zwally2012 and Schmidt2025).
ant_zone = da["zone"][:, :]
ab = NCDataset(joinpath(ant, "ANT-16KM_BASINS-IMBIE2016.nc"))
ant_basin = ab["basin"][:, :]



Zones and the IMBIE2016 basins on ANT-16KM.

title: Orbital: orbital elements and insolation
text:
The orbital elements of the Earth and insolation series computed from them, the forcing of glacial cycles. Orbital is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in Orbital/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/Orbital/Orbital-<product>.nc, each with its text form (.txt).





Product
Source
Variables
Time




Orbital-La2004
Laskar et al. (2004): La2004 orbital solution, doi:10.1051/0004-6361:20041335
ecc, obl (degree), per (degree), prec; insol_65n_jun21, insol_65n_jja, insol_65s_dec21, insol_65s_djf (W m-2)
5 Ma ago to 1 Ma in the future, 1 kyr



A series of the region “global” without a location (featureType timeSeries, dimension region, lat and lon missing). time is in years before 1950 CE (units “years ago”), negative in the future.
The insolation is the daily mean at the top of the atmosphere, computed in closed form (Berger, 1978) as in the insol library used by the models (fesmc/insol), with S0 = 1365 W m-2 and a year of 365 days with the vernal equinox on 21 March (21 June: day 172, 21 December: day 355); the seasonal means are means of the daily values (JJA: days 152-243, DJF: 335-365 and 1-59). Models that need other latitudes or days compute them from the elements, or with insol.










Source
Licence




Laskar et al. (2004), La2004
No licence stated (ASD/IMCCE); publishing assumed to be allowed

title: IceHistory: paleo ice sheets and topography
text:
Reconstructions of past ice sheets and topography (glacial cycles, Pliocene), remapped onto the grids of the domains and onto global lon-lat grids. IceHistory is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in IceHistory/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains

Batchelor et al. (2019) in the Northern Hemisphere and PaleoMIST 1.0 (Gowan et al., 2021) in the Southern Hemisphere, 0.1°, 80-21 ka (replaces Batchelor2019_ice_masks_lgc.nc of v1, used by CLIMBER-X)
f_ice_best, f_ice_min, f_ice_max, on time (years ago: 80000, 65000, 45000, 40000, 35000, 30000, 26500, 21000)
Global



Each file <GRID>_IceHistory-<Source>.nc also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and, on grids finer than the source, smoothed with a Gaussian of half the source spacing; the masks are remapped as classes (the class covering most of each cell). Ice extents from outlines (Batchelor, Margold) are rasterized as area fractions at 2 km and 1 km, so that remapping gives the fraction of each cell. The global attribute remap_method records what was done on each grid.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): elevations and thicknesses (z_*, dz_*, H_ice*) to 0.01 m; fractions (f_*) to 0.001; ages (age_*) to 3 significant digits. The masks of PRISM4 are exact.

Each file <GRID>_IceHistory-<Source>.nc also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and, on grids finer than the source, smoothed with a Gaussian of half the source spacing; the masks are remapped as classes (the class covering most of each cell). Ice extents from outlines (Batchelor, Margold) are rasterized as area fractions at 2 km and 1 km, so that remapping gives the fraction of each cell. The global attribute remap_method records what was done on each grid.

title: IceHistory: paleo ice sheets and topography
text: The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): elevations and thicknesses (z_*, dz_*, H_ice*) to 0.01 m; fractions (f_*) to 0.001; ages (age_*) to 3 significant digits. The masks of PRISM4 are exact.

title: IceChange: observed recent change of the ice sheets
text:
Observed recent change of the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets, remapped onto the grids of the domains: for now, rates of surface elevation change and ice thickness change from satellite laser altimetry; later possibly mass change, and changes of the grounding line and the ice front. IceChange is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in IceChange/remap.toml. Each source has a product per ice sheet (-ANT, -GRL), on the grids of 4 km and coarser.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




IceChange-ATL15-ANT
ICESat-2 ATL15 v6 (Smith et al., 2026): linear trend of the quarterly 1 km height change, 2019 to 2026 (cycles 03-31), doi:10.5067/ATLAS/ATL15.006
dzdt (surface elevation change rate, m yr-1)
Antarctica


IceChange-ATL15-GRL
as above, Greenland and its peripheral ice caps
dzdt
Greenland


IceChange-Smith2020-ANT
Smith et al. (2020): ICESat (2003-2009) to ICESat-2 (2018-2019), 5 km, grounded and floating ice, doi:10.1126/science.aaz5845, data http://hdl.handle.net/1773/45388
dzdt (surface elevation change rate of the grounded ice), dHdt (ice thickness change rate, ice equivalent, grounded and floating ice), m yr-1
Antarctica


IceChange-Smith2020-GRL
as above, Greenland ice sheet (grounded ice)
dzdt
Greenland



dzdt is the rate of change of the surface elevation, including the changes of the firn. dHdt is the rate of change of the ice thickness in ice equivalent: the surface elevation change corrected for changes in firn air content and, over floating ice, converted from elevation change by hydrostatic equilibrium.
ATL15 gives the height change of each quarter relative to 2020 (and rates over moving windows of up to 7 years); dzdt is the linear trend over the whole record in each 1 km cell, the unweighted least-squares fit over the quarters with data and ice in the cell, and missing where fewer than 75% of the quarters have them (e.g. moving ice fronts). The period and the number of quarters are in the global attributes of the files (2019-01-01 to 2026-04-02, 30 quarters, at least 23 valid). The trend agrees with the 7-year rates of ATL15 (dhdt_084mo; correlation 0.92-0.99 by quadrant). Integrated over the ice, dzdt is +107 km3 yr-1 in Antarctica (grounded and floating ice; East Antarctica rising, West Antarctica falling) and -206 km3 yr-1 in Greenland with its peripheral ice caps. There are no data south of about 88°S. See ATL15_dzdt.
Smith et al. (2020) give over floating ice only thickness changes, so dzdt of IceChange-Smith2020-ANT covers the grounded ice only, and dHdt both the grounded and the floating ice, which are on 5 km grids of their own in the source and are combined on each grid (see Several files): where a cell has both, their contributions add up, so that the totals of both are kept. Greenland has no dHdt, as Smith et al. (2020) have no firn correction there. There are no data south of about 86°S (not covered by ICESat). Integrated over the ice, the surface elevation change of the grounded ice of Antarctica is -130 km3 yr-1, its thickness change -127 km3 yr-1 (-116 Gt yr-1 of ice; Smith et al., 2020: -118 Gt yr-1) and that of the floating ice +16 km3 yr-1; the surface elevation change of Greenland is -250 km3 yr-1. See Smith2020_dzdt.
Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source (f_valid_<field> where the fields differ). The fields are remapped conservatively, and smoothed on the grids finer than the source (4 km, for the 5 km grids of Smith et al., 2020).



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): dzdt and dHdt to 1%; f_valid to 0.001.

title: GHG: greenhouse gases from ice cores
text:
Atmospheric CO2, CH4 and N2O over glacial cycles, from Antarctic ice cores: the records of EPICA Dome C, a composite of several cores, and spline-smoothed series with their radiative forcing. GHG is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in GHG/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/GHG/GHG-<product>.nc, each with its text form (.txt).

EDC

Köhler et al. (2017): spline-smoothed CO2, CH4 and N2O and their radiative forcing, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.871273
global
co2 (ppm), ch4, n2o (ppb), rf_co2, rf_ch4, rf_n2o (W m-2), each with _sd
2016 CE to 156 ka (N2O to 135 ka), every year



The records of EDC are time series at the site (featureType timeSeries, dimension station); the composite and the splines are series of a region without a location (dimension region, region_name, lat and lon missing). time is in years before 1950 CE (units “years ago”), the gas age on the time scale of the source (in the comment of time). The records of EDC, with depths, also have time_aicc2023, the gas age on AICC2023 (Bouchet et al., 2023) interpolated linearly in depth in the AICC2023 table of EDC (see IceCores). The composite of Bereiter et al. (2015) has no depths and is kept on its published ages. Uncertainties _sd are 1 sigma.

title: Freshwater: freshwater fluxes of the ice sheets
text:
Freshwater flux and mass anomaly series of the ice sheets by region. Freshwater is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in Freshwater/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/Freshwater/Freshwater-<product>.nc.


From Schmidt et al. (2025), doi:10.5281/zenodo.17386710, one product per series file (see Schmidt2025_fwf):








Product
Variables (by region)
Time

annual, 1840-2025

surface_runoff_from_ice, surface_runoff_from_land, subglacial_discharge_from_ice, subglacial_discharge_from_land (m3 s-1), min_discharge_depth (m)
monthly, 1950-2022


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_GL_mass_anomaly
SMB_ROI, D_ROI, MB_ROI, their anomalies *_anom, SMB_ROI_sd, D_ROI_sd, and the total MB (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1850-2024

calving, anomaly, calving_sd, baseline (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1997-2021


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_subshelf_melt
melt, anomaly, baseline (Gt yr-1), injection_depth_min, injection_depth_max (m)
annual, 1991-2021


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_grounded_mass_change
grounded_dm (Gt yr-1)
annual, 2002-2023


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_mass_anomaly
calve, subshelf_melt, grounded_loss, MB_ROI_anom (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1990-2023



The series are by region (featureType timeSeries, dimensions time and region): 7 regions in Greenland (CE, CW, NE, NO, NW, SE, SW) and 18 in Antarctica (A-Ap, …, K-A). region is the region number, the basin id of the Regions basin set Schmidt2025 (<GRID>_BASINS-Schmidt2025.nc, see Regions), so that a series can be put on the grid of a domain; region_name is its name, and lat, lon the centroid of the region. time is in days since 1800-01-01, the middle of each year or month, with time_bnds.
The normalised iceberg melt climatologies of the record (GL_iceberg_melt.nc, AQ_iceberg_melt.nc) are gridded (0.5° lon-lat) and left out: they are for ocean models, which remap them onto their own grids.

text:
From Schmidt et al. (2025), doi:10.5281/zenodo.17386710, one product per series file (see Schmidt2025_fwf):








Product
Variables (by region)
Time




Freshwater-Schmidt2025_GL_discharge
discharge, discharge_sd (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1840-2025


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_GL_runoff
surface_runoff_from_ice, surface_runoff_from_land, subglacial_discharge_from_ice, subglacial_discharge_from_land (m3 s-1), min_discharge_depth (m)
monthly, 1950-2022


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_GL_mass_anomaly
SMB_ROI, D_ROI, MB_ROI, their anomalies *_anom, SMB_ROI_sd, D_ROI_sd, and the total MB (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1850-2024


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_calving
calving, anomaly, calving_sd, baseline (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1997-2021


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_subshelf_melt
melt, anomaly, baseline (Gt yr-1), injection_depth_min, injection_depth_max (m)
annual, 1991-2021


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_grounded_mass_change
grounded_dm (Gt yr-1)
annual, 2002-2023


Freshwater-Schmidt2025_AQ_mass_anomaly
calve, subshelf_melt, grounded_loss, MB_ROI_anom (Gt yr-1)
annual, 1990-2023



The series are by region (featureType timeSeries, dimensions time and region): 7 regions in Greenland (CE, CW, NE, NO, NW, SE, SW) and 18 in Antarctica (A-Ap, …, K-A). region is the region number, the basin id of the Regions basin set Schmidt2025 (<GRID>_BASINS-Schmidt2025.nc, see Regions), so that a series can be put on the grid of a domain; region_name is its name, and lat, lon the centroid of the region. time is in days since 1800-01-01, the middle of each year or month, with time_bnds.
The normalised iceberg melt climatologies of the record (GL_iceberg_melt.nc, AQ_iceberg_melt.nc) are gridded (0.5° lon-lat) and left out: they are for ocean models, which remap them onto their own grids.

title: BasalState: basal thermal state of the ice sheets
text:
Basal temperature and basal thermal state (frozen, thawable, thawed) of the ice sheets, remapped onto the grids of the domains. BasalState is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in BasalState/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




BasalState-Dawson2022
Dawson et al. (2022): thermal steady state of the ISSM initialization of Antarctica (mesh of 0.3-50 km, interpolated to 1 km), doi:10.5281/zenodo.6870567
T_b (basal temperature, K), T_b_pmp (relative to the pressure melting point, K), basal_state (1 frozen, 2 thawable within 2 K of the pressure melting point, 3 thawed), bmelt_grnd (basal melt rate, m yr-1 ice equivalent), beta (friction coefficient of the linear sliding law tau_b = beta u_b, Pa yr m-1)
Antarctica



The basal melt rate bmelt_grnd of Dawson et al. (2022) is the model’s own result: about 21 Gt yr-1 over the grounded ice of Antarctica in total, lower than published estimates of about 65 Gt yr-1.
The fields cover the grounded ice. Continuous fields are remapped conservatively, the classes as the dominant class of each cell. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): T_b and T_b_pmp to 0.01 K; bmelt_grnd to 1%; beta to 3 significant digits; f_valid to 0.001. basal_state (classes) is exact.






Source
Licence




Dawson et al. (2022)
CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo)

title: Atmosphere: reanalysis and satellite climatologies
text:
Monthly climatologies of the atmosphere from reanalysis and satellite data, remapped onto the grids of the domains and onto global lon-lat grids. Atmosphere is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in Atmosphere/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




Atmosphere-ERA5-1981-2010, Atmosphere-ERA5-1991-2020
Hersbach et al. (2020): ERA5 monthly means, N320 Gaussian grid (about 31 km), doi:10.1002/qj.3803
zs, lsm; monthly sp, t2m, sst, u10, v10, ws10, tcc, al, tcw, tclw, tciw, pr, sf
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


Atmosphere-ERA5-plev-1981-2010, Atmosphere-ERA5-plev-1991-2020
as above, 9 pressure levels from 1000 to 500 hPa
t, z, u, v, w, uv on plev, monthly
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


Atmosphere-CERES-2001-2020
Loeb et al. (2018): CERES EBAF Ed4.2.1, 1°, doi:10.1175/JCLI-D-17-0208.1
TOA and surface radiative fluxes (W m-2), monthly
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global



On the mountain-glacier domains (Pyrenees, Patagonia, Himalaya), on their 2 km grid: Atmosphere-ERA5-1981-2010 and Atmosphere-ERA5-1991-2020; their nests and crops get these by cropping (see Nests and crops).
Winds are remapped as vectors and rotated to the axes of projected grids. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and smoothed on grids finer than the source.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): temperatures (t2m, sst, t) to 0.01 K; the elevation zs and the geopotential height z to 0.01 m; fractions (lsm, tcc, al, f_valid) to 0.001; precipitation, snowfall, winds, w and the radiative fluxes to 1%; sp, tcw, tclw and tciw to 3 significant digits.










Source
Licence




Hersbach et al. (2020), ERA5
Copernicus licence: free use and redistribution with attribution (“Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information”)


Loeb et al. (2018), CERES EBAF
NASA open data, no restrictions; cite the products

Winds are remapped as vectors and rotated to the axes of projected grids. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and smoothed on grids finer than the source.

title: Atmosphere: reanalysis and satellite climatologies
text: The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): temperatures (t2m, sst, t) to 0.01 K; the elevation zs and the geopotential height z to 0.01 m; fractions (lsm, tcc, al, f_valid) to 0.001; precipitation, snowfall, winds, w and the radiative fluxes to 1%; sp, tcw, tclw and tciw to 3 significant digits.

title: Datasets
text: Each dataset gathers products on one theme, e.g. the geothermal heat flow maps of several sources (GHF), on the grids of the domains where they apply. Topo and Regions are made by their own pipelines on every domain, from the base grid to the coarsest grid; the other gridded datasets are made by remapping published maps, on the grids that their sources resolve (see Precision and file sizes). The Records are non-gridded data (time series, sites, profiles). The page of each dataset describes its products, their sources and licences, and lists its files under Downloads; Products shows which dataset is on which domain.

title: FesmData
text: FesmData produces datasets for models, such as topography, region masks, geothermal heat flow or surface mass balance, on the grids of each model domain, from the base grid (25 m to 2 km) to 32 km, and on global lon-lat grids. Each is made from the original sources, with every step in the repository, and released on Helmholtz Codebase, one package per domain, dataset and grid, versioned by the release; releases can also be archived on Zenodo with a DOI.

title: FesmData
text:
Getting started
With Julia installed (no packages needed):
git clone https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData.git
cd FesmData
export FESMDATA=/path/to/fesmdata          # where the files go
julia fesmdata.jl list Topo                # where Topo is released
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM       # Topo on the 8 km grid of Antarctica
The files land in $FESMDATA/Antarctica/ANT-8KM/, with the grid files. See Download for the details.

title: Download
text: The products are downloaded with fesmdata.jl, a Julia script of FesmData, which puts every file in a fixed layout and checks it against its checksum. Single files can also be downloaded without it (see Single files).

title: Download
text:
Get the tool
You need Julia (a recent version; no packages to install) and a copy of FesmData. All commands are run from its folder.
git clone https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData.git
cd FesmData
julia fesmdata.jl help
git pull updates it, and with it the list of the released products.

title: Download
text:
Where the data go
The environment variable FESMDATA sets the folder for the data, e.g. in your ~/.bashrc:
export FESMDATA=/path/to/fesmdata
On Levante and Albedo, source shared/machines/<machine>.env sets it to the shared folder of the project, where the products usually are already (see Machines and storage). On macOS or Windows, do not put it next to the FesmData folder as fesmdata: on a case-insensitive file system, that is FesmData itself.
Every file goes to $FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/: one folder per domain, and in it one folder per grid with all datasets on that grid. A grid folder thus holds everything a model needs on that grid, and can be copied as a whole:
$FESMDATA/
  Antarctica/
    ANT-8KM/
      grid_ANT-8KM.txt                 grid description (cdo), of the dataset Grids
      ANT-8KM_grid.nc                  x, y, lon, lat and area of the cells, of Grids
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc    a product of the dataset Topo
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-Bedmap3.nc
      ANT-8KM_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc      a product of the dataset GHF
      ...
    ANT-16KM/
  Greenland/
    GRL-4KM/
  ...
  Records/
    IceCores/
      IceCores-Kindler2014.nc          a product of the records dataset IceCores
      IceCores-Kindler2014.txt         its text form
Domains are named after their folder (Antarctica, Greenland, Thwaites, Patagonia, …), grids after the key of their domain and their resolution (ANT-8KM, GRL-500M, DDG-25M); a grid name thus also gives its domain. See Domains and grids (or julia fesmdata.jl domains) for all domains and grids (julia fesmdata.jl where <lon> <lat>: those containing a point, with their datasets), and Products for what is released on each.

title: Download
text:
Find what is there
julia fesmdata.jl list                     # all released datasets on all domains
julia fesmdata.jl list Topo                # a dataset on all its domains (or a domain)
julia fesmdata.jl list Antarctica Topo     # a dataset on a domain: its grids and
                                           # files, their sizes, and which are here
julia fesmdata.jl list ANT-8KM             # everything on a grid
The arguments can be given in any order. list also shows the products that nests and crops get by cropping (see Nests and crops).
To find products by what they are rather than by dataset, search looks for terms in the names of the products and their files, their sources (with the titles, authors and references of their READMEs), their variables (where the definitions list them) and the domains they are released on, ignoring case and accents; a product must contain all terms:
julia fesmdata.jl search Montoya           # the products from Montoya and Levermann (2008)
julia fesmdata.jl search ghf Antarctica    # heat flow products released on Antarctica
Products not released yet are listed too, as (not released).

title: Download
text:
Download what you need
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM            # one grid
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM ANT-16KM   # several grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Antarctica Topo         # all grids of a domain
julia fesmdata.jl fetch IceCores Records        # a records dataset
fetch needs the dataset, and a domain or grids (in any order). A grid name implies its domain, so the domain can be left out when grids are given.
path prints the paths of the downloaded files of a dataset, one per line, for scripts and viewers; products can be named to keep only theirs (the files missing are counted on stderr):
julia fesmdata.jl path Topo ANT-8KM                  # all products of Topo on a grid
ncview $(julia fesmdata.jl path Topo ANT-8KM BedMachine-v4)

title: Download
text:
Nests and crops
The thematic datasets (those made by remapping: GHF, Velocity, SMB, Atmosphere, …) are released once, on the domain or crop that has them, and not again on the nests and crops inside it (e.g. Thwaites, a crop of Antarctica, or Jakobshavn, a nest of GreenlandPaleo inside its crop Greenland); a nest or crop is released with its own products only (e.g. Topo, Regions). fetch makes the others there on demand, by cropping them:
julia fesmdata.jl list Jakobshavn          # its datasets, and those by cropping
julia fesmdata.jl list Jakobshavn SMB      # the grids and files that fetch makes
julia fesmdata.jl fetch SMB Jakobshavn     # all grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch SMB JAK-4KM        # one grid
A nest or crop gets, for each thematic dataset, its own products; those of its parent domain that it does not have; and those of the crops of its parent domain that contain it (e.g. Greenland for the nests of GreenlandPaleo: MAR, Joughin2018, …) that neither has (list shows where each comes from). fetch downloads the files of these products (e.g. Greenland/SMB, to $FESMDATA/Greenland/), and cuts each to the nest or crop, as $FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<NAME>.nc with the grid files:

at a resolution of the nest or crop, on its own grid (e.g. JAK-1KM, next to its Topo and Regions, with the grid files of the grid from Grids);
at the other resolutions, on the cells of the domain grids that overlap the nest or crop (e.g. JAK-4KM, the same cells from the parent and from a crop, which lie on the parent grids).

A grid of a crop that does not cover the nest or crop is skipped, with a message (no partial crops). The crops are exact subsets of the files they are cut from (all variables, attributes and compression as they are), and record that file and its cells in their global attributes (cropped_from, cropped_from_checksum, cropped_from_release, cropped_index_xc and cropped_index_yc, 1-based). Running fetch again keeps the crops of the current files, and makes them again after a new release. A grid of the nest or crop whose released files are on another grid than in shared/domains.toml (a release made before the grid changed) stops the cropping, until it is released again. Cropping needs a few Julia packages (NCDatasets, FesmUtils), which fetch installs on first use.

title: Download
text:
Mirror everything
To keep a copy of all products on a machine (or of a dataset or a domain):
julia fesmdata.jl mirror                # everything
julia fesmdata.jl mirror Topo           # one dataset
julia fesmdata.jl mirror Antarctica     # one domain
It first checks the files present, shows what is to download or update and its size, and asks once. Run it again after new releases to update the copy: only new and changed files are downloaded (--yes skips the question, e.g. in a job). mirror also makes the products of the active nests and crops by cropping (as fetch, see Nests and crops), e.g. Stratigraphy on Greenland from GreenlandPaleo; crops already made from the current files are kept.

title: Download
text:
Archives and other folders
--dir=<folder> lists, fetches or mirrors in <folder>/<Domain>/<GRID>/ instead of $FESMDATA (FESMDATA need not be set); fetch --dir writes the crops there too. Only the latest release of each dataset is kept on Helmholtz Codebase, so to keep the releases in use before updating, mirror them into a folder first:
julia fesmdata.jl mirror --dir=/work/ba1442/fesmdata-archive/2026-10-12
julia fesmdata.jl mirror
Files already in $FESMDATA at the same release (checksums) are hard linked from there (no extra space; copied on another file system, or with --copy), the others downloaded, and the registry files of the released datasets go to <folder>/registry/, as the list of what the folder holds. Updates of $FESMDATA write new files, so the hard links keep the archived ones; tools that change files in place (e.g. ncatted) would change both: use --copy for an archive next to files that may be changed in place. Running mirror --dir again on an archive updates it to the latest releases. Earlier releases still in use are kept in such archives on the HPC systems.

title: Download
text:
Checksums and updates
Every file is checked against its checksum (sha256) after download. Files already present are kept if they are of the release, and replaced if they are of an earlier release (fetch and mirror update them); a file changed locally (not of a release) stops the download, unless --overwrite is given. list --outdated checks the files already present (of all datasets, or of a dataset, domain or grids) and lists those of earlier releases or changed locally, with the fetch commands to update them:
julia fesmdata.jl list --outdated                # everything in $FESMDATA
julia fesmdata.jl list Antarctica --outdated     # one domain

title: Download
text:
Versions and citation
Each release of a dataset has a version (e.g. Topo 2.2.0, tag topo-v2.2.0 of FesmData), shown on the Products page and by list. Every file records how it was made in its global attributes (fesmdata_version, fesmdata_commit, history), and the sources it was made from. Please cite the original datasets (see the page of each dataset), and the DOI of the release where there is one (releases can be archived on Zenodo). cite shows where the references of products are: the README of each source (references and licence), the README of the dataset, and the DOIs of the releases:
julia fesmdata.jl cite Paleoclimate CLIMBER3a-present   # one product (or several)
julia fesmdata.jl cite GHF                              # all products of a dataset

title: Download
text:
Single files
Single files can also be downloaded without the tool, from the end of the page of each dataset (Downloads) or from Helmholtz Codebase, one package per domain, dataset and grid. Download the grid files of the grid too (grid_<GRID>.txt, <GRID>_grid.nc), listed under Grid files.

title: Domains and grids
text: All datasets are made on the same model domains and grids, defined in shared/domains.toml.

title: Domains and grids
text:
Concepts
A domain is a region on a map projection (polar stereographic, transverse Mercator such as UTM, or Albers equal-area) with a base grid, its finest resolution, e.g. ANT-500M for Antarctica. The coarser grids of the domain are made from the base grid by merging whole cells, e.g. ANT-1KM to ANT-32KM. All grids of a domain are therefore nested: every coarse cell is made of whole base cells, and the datasets on them are exact conservative means of the base grid.
A crop is a smaller region inside a domain, cut from its grids, at the same resolutions or some of them, e.g. Greenland, a crop of GreenlandPaleo. Its extent is that of its grid at the base resolution; at each coarser resolution its grid is the cells of the domain grid that overlap this extent, so adding a resolution does not change the others.
A nest is a smaller domain inside a domain, on the same projection, with a finer base grid of its own, made from the sources like any domain, e.g. Jakobshavn (250 m) in GreenlandPaleo (500 m). At the resolutions it shares with its parent, its grids are the cells of the parent grids that overlap its extent, so that its 500 m grid is a part of GRL-PAL-500M.
A domain is active if its products are made and released. An inactive domain is defined, but left out of the releases (see Inactive domains).
Each domain, crop and nest has an output folder under $FESMDATA, which is also its name in fesmdata.jl and on the website (e.g. Antarctica, Thwaites), and a key, the prefix of the names of its grids (e.g. ANT, THW).

title: Domains and grids
text:
Ice-sheet domains and nests
Antarctica (ANT, 500 m to 32 km), GreenlandPaleo (GRL-PAL, 500 m to 32 km; Greenland and the surrounding ocean and land, for glacial cycles) and North (NH, 2-32 km; the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets) are on polar stereographic projections. Greenland (GRL) is a crop of GreenlandPaleo, and Laurentide (LIS) and Eurasia (EIS) are crops of North.
The crops of Antarctica and the nests of Greenland cover single drainage basins, with their ice shelves or fjords and 50 km around them: in Antarctica the Amundsen Sea Embayment (ASE, at 500 m to 32 km), the Thwaites (THW) and Pine Island (PIG) glaciers, the Filchner-Ronne (FRIS), Ross (ROSS) and Amery (AMY) ice shelves with the grounded ice within 300 km upstream of them, and the Wilkes Subglacial Basin (WSB), at 500 m and 1 km; in Greenland Jakobshavn Isbrae (JAK), the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream (NEGIS), and the Petermann (PET) and Helheim (HEL) glaciers, at 250 m, 500 m and 1 km.

title: Domains and grids
text:
Mountain-glacier domains
The mountain-glacier domains cover the extent of their glaciers at the Last Glacial Maximum, each on the projection used for glacier modelling in its region, with base grids of 250 m (500 m for Svalbard) and a 2 km grid:

Pyrenees (PYR, UTM 31N).
Patagonia (PAT, UTM 18S), from 38°S to Cape Horn, with crops of the Northern and Southern Patagonian Icefields (NPI, SPI, 250 m), nests of single icefields at 50, 100 and 250 m: Gran Campo Nevado (GCN), the Cordillera Darwin Icefield (CDI) and Monte Sarmiento (SAR), and nests at 25, 50, 100 and 250 m of the San Rafael Glacier (SRG, whose 250 m grid is the v1 SRG-250M grid) and the Schiaparelli Glacier (SCH, Monte Sarmiento).
Himalaya (HIM, Albers equal-area of High Mountain Asia), the Himalaya, Karakoram and Hindu Kush, with a nest of the Drang Drung Glacier (DDG, Zanskar) at 25, 50, 100 and 250 m.
Alps (ALP, UTM 32N).
Svalbard (SVB, UTM 33N).
New Zealand (NZ, NZTM2000).

title: Domains and grids
text:
Global grids
The Global domain (GLOBAL) has global lon-lat grids at 0.1°, 0.25°, 0.5°, 1°, 2° and 5° (GLOBAL-0.1DEG, …, GLOBAL-5DEG), each with cell edges at -180° and -90°. They are not nested (0.25° is not a multiple of 0.1°). It also has Gaussian grids, named by their spectral truncation, e.g. GLOBAL-T170 (512 x 256, as used by VILMA), made only for the products that need them. Global sources are remapped onto these grids, so that all global products share them.

title: Domains and grids
text:
Grid names and grid files
Grids are named after the key of their domain (or crop, or nest) and their resolution: ANT-8KM, GRL-PAL-500M, DDG-25M, GLOBAL-0.5DEG. A grid name thus also gives its domain. Every grid has its own folder, with its grid files and all datasets on that grid:
$FESMDATA/<folder>/<GRID>/
    grid_<GRID>.txt         grid description (cdo)
    <GRID>_grid.nc          x, y, lon, lat and area of the cells
    <GRID>_TOPO-<product>.nc, <GRID>_REGIONS.nc, <GRID>_GHF-<source>.nc, ...
The grid files are released once per grid, in the dataset Grids, for all datasets on the grid: fetch gets them with the products of any dataset. To get only the grid files of a domain, or of a grid:
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Grids Antarctica
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Grids ANT-8KM
They are released on the grids with products of at least one dataset (Grids in the table above links to those of each domain), and listed below. The other grids (e.g. the grids of a nest at the resolutions of its parent, which get their products by cropping) get their grid files from fetch, which writes them with the crops. The grid files are written by Topo step 1 on the projected grids, and by fesmdata.jl remap on the global grids (see Grids/README.md).

title: Domains and grids
section: Which datasets are on which grids
text:
Which datasets are on which grids
Topo and Regions are made on every grid of every active domain, crop and nest, from the high-resolution sources. Regions also has the masks of the nests and crops of a domain on all grids of the domain, its crops and nests (<GRID>_DOMAINS.nc, see Regions).
The thematic datasets (GHF, Velocity, SMB, …) are made by remapping published maps, which are much coarser than the base grids. They are made only on the grids that add information: as a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the spacing of the source, e.g. 16 km and 0.5° for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° for sources at 0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most others, and the 2 km grids of the mountain-glacier domains. A model that needs a finer grid can remap online.
They are released on the domains, and on the crops that a product lists (e.g. Greenland, Laurentide and Eurasia, or a Greenland-only source on Greenland). The other crops and the nests lie on the grids of their domain, so they get the thematic datasets by cropping those of their domain (or of a crop that contains them, e.g. Greenland for Jakobshavn), on demand, when they are downloaded (see Nests and crops). Products shows which dataset is on which domain.

title: Domains and grids
text:
Inactive domains
A domain can be defined but not used yet (active = false in shared/domains.toml; none at present): its grids and products are made only on request, and it is left out of the releases and figures. To have one made and released, open an issue.

title: Precision and file sizes
text: FesmData puts many datasets on many grids, from 25 m to 5°. To keep the releases small enough to download and store, the files are made only on the grids that need them, and their values are rounded to a precision well below the uncertainty of the data. None of this changes how the files are read: they are ordinary NetCDF-4 files with Float32 and integer variables.

title: Precision and file sizes
text:
Resolution
A thematic dataset (GHF, SMB, Velocity, …) is made only on grids that add information: as a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the spacing of its source, e.g. 16 km and 0.5° for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° for sources at 0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most others. A finer grid of a coarse source would only be large; a model that needs it can remap online. Topo and Regions, made from high-resolution sources, are on all grids. The nests and crops of a domain get the thematic datasets by cropping those of the domain (see Domains).

title: Precision and file sizes
text:
Precision
Each float field is rounded on output to a tolerance that depends on its kind, well below the uncertainty of the data: the mantissa bits of each value that are not needed for that tolerance are set to zero (bit rounding), which compresses much better. The values stay Float32, and missing values are kept.

3 significant digits (0.05%)



The first row that matches a field applies. Integer fields (masks, classes, region numbers) are never rounded. A relative tolerance holds for each value; for an absolute tolerance, the bits kept are set by the largest magnitude of the field, so that every value is within it; most errors are well below the tolerance. The coarser Topo grids and the ensemble products are made from rounded files and rounded again, so their error can exceed the tolerance slightly. The page of each dataset gives the precision of its fields.

title: Precision and file sizes
Precision and file sizes
text:
Compression
With the rounding, the fields are compressed with deflate level 4 (with shuffle). The files are 1.4-1.5 times smaller than lossless files for Topo, and 2.4-4.6 times for Regions and the thematic datasets (e.g. 3.3 for Velocity, 3.9 for SMB).
If a field needs a finer precision for your use, open an issue.

title: Precision and file sizes
text:
For maintainers
The tolerances are set in shared/precision.jl. A field that needs a finer precision (or allows a coarser one) gets an exception in its product: precision in <Dataset>/remap.toml, e.g. precision = { ghf = 0.1, smb = "1%", lat = "lossless" } (see Adding a dataset). A domain may set another tolerance of elevations and thicknesses (elevation_precision in shared/domains.toml); none does. Intermediate files of the pipelines are not rounded.

title: BasalMelt: ice-shelf basal melt rates
text:
Basal melt rates of ice shelves from observations, remapped onto the grids of the domains. BasalMelt is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in BasalMelt/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




BasalMelt-Adusumilli2020
Adusumilli et al. (2020): 500 m basal melt rates of the Antarctic ice shelves, mean 2010-2018, from CryoSat-2, doi:10.6075/J04Q7SHT
bmelt (gaps filled with the mean rate at the same ice draft), bmelt_cs2 (CryoSat-2 only), bmelt_err (uncertainty), m yr-1 ice equivalent, positive for melting
Antarctica


BasalMelt-Adusumilli2020-heights
Adusumilli et al. (2020): quarterly height changes of the Antarctic ice shelves 1992-2018 from radar altimetry, 10 km (not melt rates; grids of 8 km and coarser), doi:10.6075/J04Q7SHT
dh_alt (surface height), dh_firn (firn air content), m, relative to 1994; smb_discharge (surface mass balance and discharge change, m yr-1 ice equivalent); on time (quarters); no uncertainties (inconsistent in the source file)
Antarctica


BasalMelt-Rignot2013
Rignot et al. (2013): 1 km basal melt rates of the Antarctic ice shelves in 2007-2008, doi:10.5061/dryad.5hqbzkhg2
bmelt (actual), bmelt_ss (steady state), m yr-1 ice equivalent, positive for melting; their means over the drainage basins (Zwally et al., 2012) bmelt_basin, bmelt_eq_basin, and bmelt_reese, bmelt_eq_reese over groups of them (as bm_ac_reese, bm_eq_reese of v1)
Antarctica



Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source (the ice shelves). Fields are remapped conservatively. The basin means of BasalMelt-Rignot2013 are one value per basin, taken on the source grid over the ice shelves of the basin (basin 25, without data, over those of basins 24 and 26), and set on every cell of the basin on each grid, the cells outside the basins (open ocean, outer cells) taking the nearest basin: they cover the whole grid (see Rignot2013_bmelt).
BasalMelt-Adusumilli2020-heights has the height changes from which Adusumilli et al. (2020) derive time series of melt rates (relative to the 2010-2018 mean, their Eq. S7), not melt rates: see Adusumilli2020_bmelt.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): melt rates (bmelt*, smb_discharge) to 1%; the height changes dh_alt and dh_firn to 0.01 m; f_valid to 0.001.

title: GHF: geothermal heat flow
text:
Geothermal heat flow (mW m-2) from published maps, remapped onto the grids of the domains and onto global lon-lat grids. GHF is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in GHF/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




GHF-Lucazeau2019
Lucazeau (2019): 0.5° global map fitted to heat flow observations, doi:10.1029/2019GC008389
ghf, ghf_sd (standard deviation)
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


GHF-Martos2017
Martos et al. (2017): 15 km map of Antarctica from airborne magnetic data (Curie depth), doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.882503
ghf, ghf_sd (uncertainty), depth_curie, depth_curie_sd (km)
Antarctica


GHF-Martos2018
Martos et al. (2018): 15 km map of Greenland (land only) from magnetic Curie depths, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.892973
ghf, ghf_sd (uncertainty), depth_curie, depth_curie_sd (km)
Greenland


GHF-HazzardRichards2024
Hazzard and Richards (2024): 0.5° map of Antarctica inferred from seismic velocities, doi:10.1029/2023GL106274
ghf, ghf_sd (standard deviation)
Antarctica


GHF-Davies2013
Davies (2013): 2° global map from observations, geology and young-ocean cooling, doi:10.1002/ggge.20271
ghf (mean), ghf_median, ghf_err (error estimate)
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


GHF-Shapiro2004
Shapiro and Ritzwoller (2004): 1° global map extrapolated with a seismic model, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2004.04.011
ghf, ghf_sd (standard deviation)
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


GHF-Loesing2021
Lösing and Ebbing (2021): machine-learning map of Antarctica, about 55 km, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.930237
ghf, ghf_min, ghf_max (range of alternative models)
Antarctica


GHF-Stal2020
Stål et al. (2021): Aq1, 20 km map of Antarctica, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.924857
ghf, ghf_unc (uncertainty)
Antarctica


GHF-Colgan2021
Colgan and Wansing (2021): machine-learning map of Greenland, about 55 km, doi:10.22008/FK2/F9P03L
ghf, ghf_min, ghf_max (ensemble range)
Greenland


GHF-FoxMaule2005
Fox Maule et al. (2005): map from satellite magnetic data (Curie depth), updated with the MF7 model, about 170 km, land only, doi:10.1126/science.1106888
ghf
Antarctica (no data south of 87.75°S), GreenlandPaleo, Greenland


GHF-Colgan2021-topocorr-GRL
Colgan et al. (2021): relative topographic correction at 150 m (BedMachine), doi:10.22008/FK2/BQGYYG
ghf_corr, ghf_corr_unc (dimensionless)
Greenland


GHF-Colgan2021-topocorr-ANT
Colgan et al. (2021): relative topographic correction at 500 m (BedMachine), doi:10.22008/FK2/BQGYYG
ghf_corr, ghf_corr_unc (dimensionless)
Antarctica



On the mountain-glacier domains (Pyrenees, Patagonia, Himalaya), on their 2 km grid: GHF-Lucazeau2019, GHF-Davies2013 and GHF-Shapiro2004; their nests and crops get these by cropping (see Nests and crops).
The topographic correction of Colgan et al. (2021) is not a heat flow but a dimensionless relative correction (about 0 on average), to be applied to any heat flow product as corrected heat flow = (1 + ghf_corr) × ghf (higher heat flow in valleys, lower on ridges). It is made on all grids, as it resolves the bed topography finer than any of them.
Each file <GRID>_GHF-<Source>.nc also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Each source is remapped conservatively; on grids finer than the source it is then smoothed with a Gaussian of half the source spacing (about 28 km for 0.5°), so that its cells do not show as steps. The global attribute remap_method records what was done on each grid.
GHF-Martos2018 covers the land of Greenland only: ghf and ghf_sd are filled where there are no source data (cells at the ice margin, the ocean and the rest of the grid) by harmonic interpolation (fill, mask = "all", marked by mask_fill; see Gap filling), so that they cover the whole grid. depth_curie and depth_curie_sd are not filled.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): the heat flow and its uncertainties and ranges (mW m-2) to 1%; depth_curie and depth_curie_sd (km) to 3 significant digits; ghf_corr, ghf_corr_unc (dimensionless) and f_valid to 0.001.

On the mountain-glacier domains (Pyrenees, Patagonia, Himalaya), on their 2 km grid: GHF-Lucazeau2019, GHF-Davies2013 and GHF-Shapiro2004; their nests and crops get these by cropping (see Nests and crops).
The topographic correction of Colgan et al. (2021) is not a heat flow but a dimensionless relative correction (about 0 on average), to be applied to any heat flow product as corrected heat flow = (1 + ghf_corr) × ghf (higher heat flow in valleys, lower on ridges). It is made on all grids, as it resolves the bed topography finer than any of them.
Each file <GRID>_GHF-<Source>.nc also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Each source is remapped conservatively; on grids finer than the source it is then smoothed with a Gaussian of half the source spacing (about 28 km for 0.5°), so that its cells do not show as steps. The global attribute remap_method records what was done on each grid.
GHF-Martos2018 covers the land of Greenland only: ghf and ghf_sd are filled where there are no source data (cells at the ice margin, the ocean and the rest of the grid) by harmonic interpolation (fill, mask = "all", marked by mask_fill; see Gap filling), so that they cover the whole grid. depth_curie and depth_curie_sd are not filled.

title: GHF: geothermal heat flow
text: The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): the heat flow and its uncertainties and ranges (mW m-2) to 1%; depth_curie and depth_curie_sd (km) to 3 significant digits; ghf_corr, ghf_corr_unc (dimensionless) and f_valid to 0.001.

Make a folder for the source with a prepare.jl and a README.md (see Sources), e.g. Lucazeau2019_ghf/.
Add a table [products.<Name>] to GHF/remap.toml with source, file, variables and grids (and method or smooth if the defaults do not fit).
Add it to the table of products above, and run julia fesmdata.jl remap GHF <Name>.
Release a new version of GHF (see Releasing).

title: GPS: vertical land motion
text:
Vertical velocities of GPS stations as observational estimates of glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) uplift rates. GPS is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in GPS/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/GPS/GPS-<product>.nc.





Product
Source
Sites
Variables

uplift_rate, uplift_rate_sd (mm yr-1)

title: IceCores: ice core records
text:
Time series at Antarctic and Greenland ice core sites over glacial cycles: water isotopes, temperature, accumulation, dust and surface elevation, and the AICC2023 ice core chronology. IceCores is a records dataset (non-gridded data, see Records): its products, defined in IceCores/records.toml, are prepared files in the form of the CF discrete sampling geometries, written to $FESMDATA/Records/IceCores/IceCores-<product>[-<part>].nc, each with its text form (.txt).





Product
Source
Sites
Variables
Time




IceCores-Jouzel2007
Jouzel et al. (2007): EPICA Dome C deuterium, doi:10.25921/8t7e-z147
EDC
dD (‰), tas_anom (K), depth
0-802 ka, 0.55 m bags (EDC3; also AICC2023)

Petit et al. (1999): Vostok deuterium, doi:10.25921/kcry-ae86
Vostok
dD (‰), tas_anom (K), depth

Dome Fuji

0-716 ka (AICC2012)

EDML

0-150 ka, 0.5 m (EDML1; also AICC2023)

WAIS Divide

0-68 ka, about 1 m tubes (WD2014; AICC2023 for 10-57 ka)

d18O (‰), depth

Lambert et al. (2012): EPICA Dome C dust flux, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.778213
EDC
dust_flux (mg m-2 yr-1), depth
0.4-801 ka, 25 years (EDC3; also AICC2023)

NGRIP1, NGRIP2, GRIP, GISP2
d18O (‰), ca (ng g-1), depth, mce
0-122 ka, 20 years (GICC05modelext; NGRIP also AICC2023)

Buizert et al. (2018): seasonal temperatures at ice core sites, doi:10.25921/psvs-yg80

tas_ann, tas_djf, tas_mam, tas_jja, tas_son (K)
22 ka to present, 20 years


IceCores-Barker2011-<part>
Barker et al. (2011): synthetic Greenland record GLT_syn from EDC, doi:10.1126/science.1203580; parts GLTsyn and events
Greenland (synthetic, no location)
glt_syn, glt_syn_hi, glt_syn_lo (‰); events: do_pick, do_pick_var
5-800 ka, 50 years (EDC3; speleothem ages to 400 ka)


IceCores-Kindler2014
Kindler et al. (2014): reconstruction from δ15N and a firn model, doi:10.5194/cp-10-887-2014
NGRIP
tas (K), acc (kg m-2 yr-1), depth
10-122 ka, 20 years (GICC05modelext)


IceCores-Gkinis2020
Gkinis et al. (2020): 0.05 m samples, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.925552
NEEM
d18O, dD (‰) with precision and accuracy offsets, depth
8-121 ka (GICC05, GICC05_modelext; also AICC2012)


IceCores-Vinther2009
Vinther et al. (2009): Holocene thinning, doi:10.1038/nature08355
Camp Century, NGRIP, GRIP, DYE-3
dz_srf, dz_srf_sd (m), z_srf (present)
11.7 ka to present, 20 years (GICC05)


IceCores-AICC2023-<core>
Bouchet et al. (2023): AICC2023 chronology, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.961017; one file per core
EDC, EDML, NGRIP, TALDICE, Vostok
age_ice_aicc2023, age_gas_aicc2023 and their _sd, age_ice_aicc2012, age_gas_aicc2012, acc, thinning, lid, delta_depth (profiles along depth)
to 813 ka (EDC)



The records are time series at fixed sites (featureType timeSeries, dimension station, with lat, lon, site_name, and z_srf where the source gives it); the AICC2023 files are profiles along depth (featureType profile); GLT_syn is a series of a region without a location. time is in years before 1950 CE (units “years ago”), on the time scale of the source (in the comment of time); ages b2k (before 2000 CE) are converted by subtracting 50. Water isotopes are in ‰ (units 1e-3); temperature anomalies tas_anom are relative to the present (see each source).
time_aicc2023: the records of EDC, EDML, TALDICE, Vostok and NGRIP with depths also have the ages on AICC2023 (Bouchet et al., 2023), interpolated linearly in depth in the AICC2023 table of the core (IceCores-AICC2023-<core>); missing outside the table. WAIS Divide has AICC2023 ages from the WAIS Divide-EDC tie points of AICC2023 (10-57 ka).

The records are time series at fixed sites (featureType timeSeries, dimension station, with lat, lon, site_name, and z_srf where the source gives it); the AICC2023 files are profiles along depth (featureType profile); GLT_syn is a series of a region without a location. time is in years before 1950 CE (units “years ago”), on the time scale of the source (in the comment of time); ages b2k (before 2000 CE) are converted by subtracting 50. Water isotopes are in ‰ (units 1e-3); temperature anomalies tas_anom are relative to the present (see each source).
time_aicc2023: the records of EDC, EDML, TALDICE, Vostok and NGRIP with depths also have the ages on AICC2023 (Bouchet et al., 2023), interpolated linearly in depth in the AICC2023 table of the core (IceCores-AICC2023-<core>); missing outside the table. WAIS Divide has AICC2023 ages from the WAIS Divide-EDC tie points of AICC2023 (10-57 ka).

title: Ocean: ocean temperature and salinity
text:
Ocean temperature and salinity from observations and reanalyses, remapped onto the grids of the domains. Ocean is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in Ocean/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




Ocean-Schmidtko2014
Schmidtko et al. (2014): Antarctic shelf bottom water (shallower than 1500 m), means 1975-2012, 0.25° x 0.125°, doi:10.1126/science.1256117
ct_bottom (conservative temperature), sa_bottom (absolute salinity), their standard deviations *_std, z_bottom (bottom depth)
Antarctica


Ocean-ORAS5-1981-2010, Ocean-ORAS5-annual
Zuo et al. (2019): ORAS5 ocean reanalysis (ECMWF), regridded to 1° by ECMWF, member opa0, doi:10.5194/os-15-779-2019
to (potential temperature, degC), so (salinity, PSU) on depth: monthly climatology 1981-2010, annual means 1979-2018; mask_ocn on depth (1 where the cell is mostly ocean, f_valid >= 0.5)
Antarctica, Greenland, GreenlandPaleo, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


Ocean-ISMIP7
Zhou et al. (2026): OCEAN ICE climatology 1972-2024 as extrapolated by ISMIP7 (Reese et al., 2026) on its 8 km x 60 m grid, doi:10.5194/essd-2025-727
to (potential temperature, degC), so (practical salinity, PSU), tf (thermal forcing, degC) on z (30 layers of 60 m, to 1800 m depth), filled everywhere; basin (IMBIE2 basins extended into the ocean, 0-15)
Antarctica



Each file also has f_valid (with the extra dimensions where the coverage differs between them, e.g. depth levels), the fraction of each cell covered by the source. Fields are remapped conservatively and smoothed on grids finer than the source.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): temperatures (to, tf, ct_bottom) to 0.01 K; z_bottom to 0.01 m; salinity (so, sa_bottom) to 3 significant digits (about 0.02 at 35); f_valid to 0.001. basin is exact.

title: Paleoclimate: simulations and reconstructions of past climates
text:
Climatologies of past climates from the PMIP model intercomparisons, CLIMBER-3α and CLIMBER-X (stadial and interstadial climates, with the transient output of their simulation), and gridded reconstructions of the deglacial climate of Greenland, remapped onto the grids of the domains. Paleoclimate is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in Paleoclimate/remap.toml.





Product
Source
Fields
Domains




Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<model>-<experiment>
PMIP3/CMIP5 (Braconnot et al., 2012, doi:10.1038/nclimate1456): climatologies of the PMIP variability database (CVDP), 8 models, experiments lgm, midHolocene, piControl
t2m_ann, t2m_djf, t2m_jja, sst_ann (degC), pr_ann, pr_djf, pr_jja (mm d-1); z_srf (m), f_land, f_ice of the model and experiment (CMIP5 fixed fields; not f_ice of FGOALS-g2 lgm, z_srf and f_land of MPI-ESM-P lgm)
Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global


Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<experiment>-mean, Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<experiment>-stdev
Ensemble mean and standard deviation of the 8 PMIP3 models, for each experiment
as the models, with n_<field>, the number of models with a value
as above


Paleoclimate-PMIP3-lgm-boundary-conditions
PMIP3 LGM boundary conditions (Abe-Ouchi et al., 2015, doi:10.5194/gmd-8-3621-2015)
dz_srf (m), f_land, f_ice
as above


Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<model>-<experiment>
PMIP4/CMIP6 (Kageyama et al., 2018, doi:10.5194/gmd-11-1033-2018): climatologies of the last 100 years, 4 models (AWI-ESM-1-1-LR, INM-CM4-8, MIROC-ES2L, MPI-ESM1-2-LR), experiments lgm, midHolocene, piControl
t2m_*, pr_* (annual, DJF, JJA, monthly), z_srf, f_land, f_ice
as above


Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<experiment>-mean, Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<experiment>-stdev
Ensemble mean and standard deviation of the 4 PMIP4 models, for each experiment
as the models, with n_<field>
as above


Paleoclimate-CLIMBER3a-<simulation>, Paleoclimate-CLIMBER3a-<simulation>-ocean
CLIMBER-3α (Montoya and Levermann, 2008, doi:10.1029/2007GL032560): present day (present) and LGM with wind stress x 1.7, weak and strong Atlantic overturning (lgm_1p7weak, lgm_1p7strong); atmosphere at 22.5° x 7.5°, ocean at 3.75°
atmosphere: t2m_ann, t2m_jja (degC), pr_ann (mm d-1), z_srf (m), f_land of the model; ocean: to (potential temperature, degC) on depth, mask_ocn

On the mountain-glacier domains (Pyrenees, Patagonia, Himalaya), on their 2 km grid: the ensemble means and standard deviations of PMIP3 and PMIP4 (-mean, -stdev; not the members); their nests and crops get these by cropping (see Nests and crops).
The model output is on the models’ own grids (some Gaussian), remapped conservatively. Products are made on grids of 8 km and coarser (16 km for the Buizert et al. time series, 32 km for CLIMBER-3α and CLIMBER-X, which are also on global grids of 1° and coarser): finer grids add no information to these sources, and models can remap them online. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. The ensemble products are made from the files of the models on each grid: in each cell, the mean or the standard deviation (population) of the models with a value there (e.g. sst_ann only over the ocean of each model), n_<field> models.



The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): temperatures to 0.01 K; precipitation to 1%; z_srf and dz_srf to 0.01 m; fractions (f_*, pr_frac*) to 0.001. The ensemble products are computed from the rounded products of their members and rounded again.
